O Nanak, without the Guru there is no honour; without honour (God's grace) no one gets across.
138.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
To hold what is given dearer than the One who gives it: know the manmukh to be such.
His understanding, his wisdom, his cleverness: in what words can they be told?
What one does sitting hidden within becomes known in all four directions.
Whoever practises dharma gets the name of the righteous; by committing sin one is known as a sinner.
O Creator, you yourself play out all these plays; what other can we name and speak of?
As long as your light is (in the body), so long it is you who speak in that light; without the light, let anyone do anything at all, and I will see and acknowledge it.
O Nanak, through the Guru the one Lord, skilful and all-knowing, has come into sight.
138.5: You yourself created the world, and you yourself set it to its worldly business.
Giving it the drugging herb of attachment, you have led the world astray from yourself.
Within (it) is the fire of craving; hungry and thirsty, (the world) is never sated.
This world is nothing but anxiety; (in it, beings) die and are born, come and go.
Without the True Guru attachment does not break; all have grown weary performing (ritual) deeds.
Through the Guru's teaching the Naam is meditated on; when it pleased you, (the soul) was sated in peace.
(Such a one) saves his whole family line; blessed is the mother who bore him.
Lovely are the glory and the understanding of one who has joined his mind to the Lord.
139.1: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Seeing without eyes, hearing without ears,
walking without feet, working without hands,
speaking without a tongue: so one dies while living.
O Nanak, it is by recognising (the Lord's) Hukam that one then meets the Master.
139.2: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
(The Lord) is seen, is heard of, is known (in his creation), yet the taste (of meeting him) is not had.
How can one who is lame, handless and blind run and fall upon (his) neck?
If one makes the fear (of God) one's feet, love one's hands, and attention (held on him) one's eyes,
says Nanak: O wise (soul-bride), in this way union with the Husband comes about.
139.3: For ever and ever you are the One; you yourself have staged the play of duality.
Creating Haumai and pride, you placed greed within beings.
Keep (them) as it pleases you; all do only what you make them do.
Some you forgive and unite with yourself; it is you who have set them in the Guru's teaching.
Some stand ready, doing your service; without the Name nothing else pleases them.
To them any other work is worthless; some you have set to the true work.
Son, wife and family are there, yet some, who are pleasing to you, stay untouched (by them).
They are pure within and without, merged in the True Name.
139.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Should I make a cave in the mountain of gold, or (dwell) in the waters of the netherworld;
whether on the earth or in the sky, should I stay upside down, on my head;
should I cover my body wholly in clothes, and make washing my constant work;
should I cry aloud the Vedas, white, red, yellow and black;
should I live filthy and grimy: (all this is) the vice of an evil understanding.
Nanak, reflecting on the Shabad, asks only this: may there be no I-ness and no me-and-mine, and may I not be (a self apart) at all.
139.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Washing his clothes, he washes his body, and thinks himself (a man of) self-restraint.
The filth stuck within he does not know; he scrubs and scrubs, washing (himself) from outside.
The blind one has strayed and fallen into the net of Jam.
He takes what belongs to another for his own, and in Haumai he suffers pain.
O Nanak, when through the Guru Haumai is broken, then one meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har;
he repeats the Naam, worships the Naam alone, and through the Naam is merged in peace.
139.6: Ordaining their union, (the Lord) has joined the body and the swan (the soul).
The very One who created (them) has also ordained (their) parting.
The fool goes on enjoying pleasures, (the root of) every pain.
From pleasure diseases arise, through the sins committed.
From joy spring sorrow and parting; so (beings) are brought forth and wasted away.
Keeping the reckonings of fools, (man) has taken on a wrangle (of birth and death).
The settlement lies in the True Guru's hands; he has put an end to the wrangle.
What the Creator does, that alone will be; (no one's) driving can drive it otherwise.
139.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who tells lies and eats carrion (what is another's by right)
is robbed himself, and has his companions robbed as well.
O Nanak, such a leader is found out.
140.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The one within whom the True One dwells utters the True Name with his mouth, and speaks the truth.
He himself walks on the Lord's path, and puts others on the Lord's path.
If what lies ahead is a place of pilgrimage (of clean, open water), the filth comes off; bathing in a stagnant pond, one gathers still more filth.
The True Guru is the perfect place of pilgrimage, who meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, night and day.
He is set free himself, with his family, and, giving the Name of the Lord, Har Har, he frees the whole world.
Servant Nanak is a sacrifice to the one who repeats (the Naam) himself and has others repeat the Naam.
140.2: Some gather roots and tubers to eat, and make their dwelling in some corner of the forest.
Some put on saffron robes and wander about as Yogis and Sannyasis.
(Yet) within them is great craving, the longing for clothes and food.
Wasting their life in vain, they are neither householders nor renunciants.
Jamkaal does not lift from their heads, (for in them is) desire of the three kinds.
Through the Guru's teaching death does not come near, when one becomes the servant of (the Lord's) servants.
With the true Shabad and the True One in the mind, one is detached while living at home.
O Nanak, those who serve their True Guru become free of (worldly) hopes.
140.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If blood stains the clothes, the garment becomes unclean;
those who drink the blood of men, how can their mind be pure?
Says Nanak: take the name of God on your lips with a clean heart;
all else is the world's show, and (by it) you do false deeds.
140.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
When I am nothing (within), what can I tell (others)? With no virtue in me, what can I make myself out to be?
Through what I do and what I say, I am full (of filth); again and again I am soiled, and I wash.
I do not understand myself, yet I make the people understand: such is the leader I become.
O Nanak, one who, being blind himself, shows (others) the way has all his companions robbed.
Going on ahead (to the world beyond), he is struck again and again on the face: then such a leader is found out.
140.5: In all the months and seasons, in every ghari and muhurat, you are to be contemplated.
By calculations (of lucky days) no one has found you, O True One, unseen and infinite.
The learned man in whom are greed, avarice and pride is to be called a fool.
It is the Name that should be read, the Name that should be understood, reflecting through the Guru's teaching.
Those who through the Guru's teaching have earned the wealth of the Naam have their storehouses filled with devotion.
Those who have accepted the pure Naam are found true at the door of the True One.
The One whose are the soul and the breath of life: his infinite light is within (every being).
You alone are the true banker; the rest of the world are pedlars.
140.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Make compassion your mosque, faith your prayer mat, and honest, lawful earning your Quran;
modesty your circumcision, a gentle nature your fast: in this way become a Muslim.
(Make) good conduct your Kaaba, truth your Pir, and good deeds your kalma and namaz;
(let) what pleases him be your rosary: (then), O Nanak, he keeps your honour.
141.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, what is another's by right is (as) the pig to the one (the Muslim) and the cow to the other (the Hindu).
The Guru, the Pir, will vouch (for one) only if one does not eat carrion.
No one goes to paradise by talk; one is saved by practising truth.
Put spices into what is forbidden, and it still does not become lawful.
O Nanak, by false talk only falsehood is gained.
141.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The prayers are five, their times are five, and the five have five names.
(Let) the first be truth, the second lawful earning, the third (asking) God for the good of all;
the fourth a clean intention and mind, the fifth the praise and glory (of God).
Reciting the kalma of good conduct, one may then call oneself a Muslim.
O Nanak, as many as are false (to these), the honour of the false is false.
141.3: Some trade in jewels and precious things, some deal in glass.
When the True Guru is pleased, the stores of jewels within are found.
Without the Guru no one has found them; the blind, the false, have died barking (from door to door).
The manmukhs have rotted away in duality and died; they do not understand (true) reflection.
Apart from the One there is no other; before whom can they cry out?
Some, without wealth, are ever barking (from door to door); the coffers of some are full.
Without the Name there is no other wealth; all the rest is poison (of Maya), mere ashes.
O Nanak, (the Lord) himself causes (all) to be done and himself does (all); by his Hukam he sets (all) right.
141.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
To be called a Muslim is hard; if one truly is one, then let one be called a Muslim.
First of all, let him hold the faith dear, and, as a burnisher scrapes off rust, let his possessions go from him.
Becoming a Muslim under the guidance of the faith, let him put away the delusion of death and life.
Let him accept the Lord's will upon his head, hold the Creator (as the doer of all), and lose his self.
Then, O Nanak, if he is merciful to all beings, let him be called a Muslim.
141.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
If one forsakes lust, anger, falsehood and slander, gives up Maya and does away with pride;
if, giving up lust, he gives up attachment to woman, then amid the black stain (anjan) of Maya he finds the Immaculate (Lord);
if, giving up vanity and pride and the love of son and wife, giving up thirst and hope, he fixes his attention on the Lord (Ram),
(then,) O Nanak, the True One comes to dwell in the mind, and through the true Shabad he merges in the Lord's Name.
141.6: Kings, subjects, chiefs: none will remain.
Shops, cities and bazaars will fall by (his) Hukam.
The strong and handsome gateways the fool thinks his own.
Storehouses full of riches are emptied in an instant.
Arab horses, chariots, camels, elephants with their trappings,
gardens, lands, houses and homes: where are they, that (he thought) his own?
(Where are) the tents, the beds of woven tape, the screens of red satin?
O Nanak, the Giver alone is true, ever-abiding; he is recognised through his creation.
141.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Should the rivers become cows, and the springs turn to milk and ghee;
should the whole earth become sugar, and (my) soul rejoice every day;
should the mountain turn to gold and silver, set with diamonds and rubies:
even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane.
142.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If the eighteen loads (all plant life) became fruit, rich and melting in taste,
if the moon and the sun, both ever circling, were held still, and my seat became unshakeable,
even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane.
142.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If pain were to strike my body, and the two ill-omened planets, Rahu (and Ketu, were set upon me),
if bloodthirsty kings were set over my head, and (your) love were shown (to me) in this form,
even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane.
142.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If fire and frost were my clothing, and wind my food,
if the enchanting women of heaven were (mine) — O Nanak, all of it must pass away —
even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane.
142.4: One who does evil in secret does not know the Master (to be present);
he is called mad, (for) he does not know his own self.
Strife is an evil thing in the world; in quarrelling one wastes away.
Without the Name, one is consumed in evil and in wandering doubt.
There are two paths; the one who knows the One will come through.
The speaker of kufr (falsehood) will burn, sunk in his kufr.
The whole world is glorious and wondrous if one is merged in the True One;
one comes through at (the Lord's) door, in (his) court, if one sheds the self.
142.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
He alone has lived in whose mind that (Lord) dwells;
O Nanak, no one else (truly) lives.
If (one empty of the Name) lives at all, he goes with his honour stripped from him;
all that he eats is forbidden.
His delight is in power, his delight in wealth;
steeped in that delight, he dances without shame.
O Nanak, he is cheated and plundered;
without the Name, he has lost his honour and gone.
142.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What comes of eating (rich food), what of wearing (fine clothes),
when that True One is not in the mind?
What are dried fruits, what is ghee and sweet gur, what fine flour, what meat?
What are clothes, what a soft bed, and the pleasures and delights enjoyed (on it)?
What are armies, what mace-bearers and attendants, and coming to dwell in palaces?
O Nanak, without the True Name, all this array is perishable.
142.7: What lies in the hands of caste? It is truth that is assayed.
If poison is in the hand, one dies on tasting it (whatever one's caste).
The rule of the True One is known (to be so) in every age.
One who obeys (his) Hukam is a chief at (his) door, in (his) court.
Obeying the command is the task for which the Master has sent (us into the world).
The drummer (the Guru) has sounded this thought through the Shabad.
Some have mounted, some have saddled (their horses);
some have tied up their loads, some have galloped away.
142.8: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
When (the crop) ripened, it was cut; only the stubble and the hedge were left standing.
Bearded ears and all, it was threshed, and the grain was taken out by winnowing away the straw.
Setting together the two stones of the mill, (people) came and sat down to grind.
Those (grains) that stayed at the door (of the mill) were saved; O Nanak, a marvel has been seen.
142.9: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
See how the sweet (cane) is cut down; cut and stripped, it is bound with ropes into bundles.
Laying it between the press's wooden rollers, strong men deal out (as it were) its punishment.
The juice pressed out is poured into the cauldron; it heats and (as it were) wails.
Even the crushed pulp is gathered up and burnt in the fire (beneath the cauldron).
Says Nanak, for sweetness one is brought to ruin (like this); come, people, and see.
143.1: Some do not keep death in mind; their hopes are many.
Day after day they die and are born again, and belong to no one.
In their own mind and heart they call themselves good;
(but) the King of Death keeps those manmukhs in his sight, day after day.
The manmukhs are false to the salt they eat; they have not known what (the Lord has done for them).
They bow only under constraint, and so do not please the Master.
The one who meets the True One, with the Name on his lips, will please the Master;
(all) will salute him on his throne; he will receive what was written (for him).
143.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What harm can water too deep to stand in do a fish? What harm can the sky do a bird?
What harm can frost do a stone? What does married home life mean to a eunuch?
Smear a dog with sandalwood, and its nature is still a dog's.
If a deaf man is instructed, and the Simritis are recited (to him),
if a blind man is kept in the light, with fifty lamps burning,
if gold is laid before a grazing herd, it still picks out the grass and eats it,
if iron is put (in the fire) to be reduced to calx, it melts, but it does not turn into cotton:
O Nanak, such are the ways of a fool; whenever he speaks, it is ever to (someone's) harm.
143.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If bronze or gold or iron cracks,
the smith joins it again with fire.
If a husband breaks with his wife,
in the world the bond is formed again through sons.
The king makes his demand; when it is given, the bond is formed.
For the hungry, the bond (with life) is formed when they eat.
Famines are mended by rivers in spate and pouring rain.
The bond of love is formed by sweet words.
One is bound to the Vedas (the scriptures) when one speaks the truth.
The dead stay bound (to the world) by the good and the charity (they did).
By such bonds the world goes on.
For a fool, the bond is formed by blows to his face.
through praise (of the Lord), the bond is formed at his court.
143.4: God himself fashions the creation, and himself takes thought (for it).
Some are counterfeit, some genuine; he himself is the one who assays.
The genuine go into (his) treasury; the counterfeit are cast outside.
The counterfeit are flung out of the True Court; to whom can they cry out?
If they run and fall in behind the True Guru, that is the excellent course.
The True Guru makes the counterfeit genuine; through the Shabad he sets (them) right.
Through love and devotion for the Guru, (they) are accepted in the True Court.
What reckoning can anyone make of those whom the Creator himself has forgiven?
143.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The whole world, pirs, sheikhs and rajas, (all go) beneath the earth;
emperors pass away; God alone abides, ever greater.
143.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Neither gods nor demons nor men,
nor Siddhas nor seekers (stay) on the earth.
The One alone is; who else is there?
144.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
nor the seven (nether worlds) under the earth (endure).
The One alone is; who else is there?
144.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the sphere of the heavens,
nor the seven continents, nor the waters,
nor food nor wind: none of them is lasting.
144.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Sustenance lies in no one's hand (but yours);
for all, hope in the One is enough.
The One alone is; who else is there?
144.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Birds have no gold tied in a knot of cloth;
they look in hope to the trees and the water;
144.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, what is inscribed on the brow
He alone puts power (into beings), and he alone takes it away.
144.6: (O Lord,) your Hukam is true and abiding; it is known through the Guru.
By the Guru's teaching, shedding the self, the True One is recognised.
True is your court; the Shabad is the pass (that admits one there).
Reflecting on the true Shabad, (the Gurmukhs) merge in the True One.
The manmukhs ever deal in falsehood, gone astray in doubt.
Their dwelling is in filth; they have never known the relish (of the Name).
Without the Name, they come and go in pain.
O Nanak, the Assayer is (the Lord) himself, who has told the counterfeit from the genuine.
144.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Lions, hawks, falcons and kuhi hawks: these (God, if he wills,) feeds on grass;
those who eat grass he feeds on meat: such are the ways he sets going.
He brings sandbanks into view in the midst of rivers, and turns dry plains into bottomless waters.
He sets a worm upon a throne, and turns armies to ashes.
All the beings that live, live by drawing breath; (but if) he keeps (one) alive, what (need is there) of breath?
O Nanak, just as it pleases the True One, so he gives (each) its morsel.
144.8: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Some feed on flesh, some eat grass;
some receive the thirty-six (kinds of) nectar-sweet foods;
some, dwelling in the earth, eat earth;
some, the counters of breath (who practise pranayama), are bent on counting their breaths;
some, devoted to the Formless One, rest on the support of the Name.
The Giver lives on; no one dies (for want of food).
O Nanak, they are robbed in whose mind he does not dwell.
144.9: The work the Perfect Guru sets is done only through (God's) grace.
Through the Guru's teaching one sheds self-conceit and meditates on the Naam.
Taken up with any other work, one wastes one's life.
Without the Name, whatever one wears and eats is all poison.
Praising the True Shabad, one merges in the True One.
Without serving the True Guru there is no dwelling in peace; one comes (into birth) again and again.
The world is counterfeit capital; (trading with it) one earns falsehood alone.
O Nanak, praising the True One, the genuine, one departs with honour.
144.10: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) if it pleases you, (beings) play music and sing; if it pleases you, they bathe in (holy) waters.
When it pleases you, they smear (their bodies with) ashes and sound the call of the horn (singi).
When it pleases you, they read the Kateb and are called mullahs and sheikhs.
When it pleases you, they become kings and enjoy flavours of every kind in plenty.
When it pleases you, they wield the sword, and heads are severed from necks.
When it pleases you, they go to foreign lands, and hearing (their) news, come back home.
When it pleases you, they are absorbed in the Name; those who walk in your will are dear to you.
Nanak offers one prayer: all the others practise only falsehood.
145.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) since you are great, all greatness is (yours); from the good, only good comes.
Since you are true, everyone is true; no one at all is false.
Speaking, seeing, talking, walking, living and dying: (all this is the spread of) Maya.
Having fashioned his Hukam, he keeps (all) within the Hukam; O Nanak, (it is) the True One himself (who does so).
145.2: Serving the True Guru without reserve, one dispels doubt.
The work the True Guru bids is the work to be done.
When the True Guru is merciful, the Naam is meditated on.
The profit of devotion is the highest (profit), and it is found through the Guru.
As a manmukh, one lives in falsehood and darkness, and earns falsehood alone.
Going to the door of the True One, one utters the Truth (the True Name).
(Then,) through the Truth, one is called within the mansion of the True One.
O Nanak, one who ever holds fast to the Truth is truthful, and merges in the True One.
145.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Kalyug is a knife, kings are butchers; dharma has grown wings and flown away.
Falsehood is the dark night of the new moon; the moon of truth is not seen to have risen anywhere.
I have searched (for it) until I am bewildered;
in the darkness no path is (to be seen).
Caught in Haumai, (the world) weeps over its pain.
Says Nanak, by what means can (it) be set free?
145.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Kalyug, (the Lord's) praise is the light shining forth in the world.
(But) only some rare one crosses over (the darkness) through the Guru.
The one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace, to him he gives (this light);
O Nanak, through the Guru that one receives the jewel (of the Name).
145.5: Between the devotees and the worldly there has never been a match.
The Creator himself makes no mistake; no one can lead him into error.
The devotees he has himself united (with him), who have practised truth and truth alone.
The worldly he has himself led astray, who, speaking falsehood again and again, have eaten poison.
They do not grasp that they must depart; they have let the poison of lust and anger grow.
The devotees serve the Lord, who have meditated on the Naam night and day.
Those who, becoming the servants of (his) servants, have rid themselves of self from within,
at the Master's door their faces are bright; the True Shabad has made them beautiful.
145.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those who in the early morning praised (the Lord) and meditated on (him) with a single mind:
they alone are the perfect shahs (the truly rich), who at the proper hour fought (their own mind) unto death.
In the second (watch) many paths (open), and the mind's thoughts are scattered.
Many fall into the fathomless (sea of the world); they go under and cannot get out.
In the third (watch) morsels go into mouths; hunger and thirst both bark (for more).
What is eaten turns to ash, yet the friendship with eating (remains).
In the fourth (watch) drowsiness comes; shutting his eyes, (man) passes as if into the other world (of deep sleep).
Rising again, he starts up the strife, (as though) he had marked out an arena for a hundred years (of life).
Every hour and every moment (is blessed), if through all eight watches there is the fear (of God).
O Nanak, (if) the Master dwells in the mind, (that) is the true bathing.
146.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
They alone are the perfect shahs who have found the Perfect One.
Through all eight watches they stay free of care, (dyed) in the love of the One.
Rare are those found (absorbed) in the sight and the form of the Unfathomable.
By perfect grace (one meets) the Perfect Guru, whose word is perfect.
O Nanak, if the Perfect One makes (someone) perfect, (that one's) weight does not fall short.
146.2: (O Lord,) when you are (mine), what need have I of anyone else? I tell the truth.
(But the soul-bride) robbed by the thief of worldly affairs does not find (the Lord's) mansion.
Because of this hard heart, (her) service is wasted.
The body in which the Truth is not found is broken and shaped (again and again).
How can (it) weigh true in the balance against the full weight?
No one calls (it) short, if Haumai is gone (from within).
The genuine, once assayed, are taken in at the door of the All-seeing One.
This merchandise is had at one shop alone: from the Perfect Guru.
146.3: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The eight watches are eight parts (of time); the ninth part is the body.
In it is the one Naam, the nine treasures; (the fortunate) seek (there) the Lord, deep in virtues.
The fortunate have praised (him), O Nanak, taking the Guru as their pir.
In the fourth watch, as morning nears, a longing wells up in those whose awareness is awake.
Their friendship is with the rivers (of the holy company), and the True Name is in their mind and on their lips.
There the Amrit (of the Name) is shared out; by (his) grace the gift is received.
The body, (like) gold, is tried on the touchstone, and takes on a fine lustre.
If the Assayer's glance of grace is on it, it is not put to the fire again.
In the (other) seven watches, truthful living is good, and one should sit with the learned.
There (in their company) sin and virtue are weighed, and the capital of falsehood runs down.
There the counterfeit are thrown out, and the genuine are praised.
To speak (of one's woes) is idle, O Nanak; pain and pleasure are in the Master's hands.
146.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Air is the Guru, water the father, and the earth the great mother.
Day and night are the two nurses, the female and the male; the whole world plays (in their care).
In (God's) presence, Dharam (Raj) reads out the good deeds and the bad.
By their own deeds, some are near (God) and some far.
Those who meditated on the Naam have gone, their toil accomplished.
O Nanak, their faces are bright, and many others have been set free along with them.
146.5: The True Guru has shown that love (for the Lord) is the true food.
(One who takes this food) is content in the True One alone, and blossoms in the True One.
In the true fortress, the true village, in his own home, he dwells.
Through the True Guru's favour (comes) the Name, and one rejoices in (the Lord's) love.
No one reaches the court of the True One by falsehood.
Uttering lie upon lie, one loses that mansion.
With the True Shabad as one's pass, no barrier is met (on the way).
Hearing, understanding and uttering the Truth, one is called into (the Lord's) mansion.
147.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If I were to wear fire, build my house in snow, and make iron my food;
if I drank down all sorrows like water, and moved the earth at my call;
if I set the sky on a balance and weighed it, with a tank (a tiny weight) on the other pan;
if I grew so vast that I could not be contained, and led everyone by a nose-string;
if there were such power in my mind that I could do (anything) myself and have it done at my word:
as great as the Master is, so great are his gifts; (were) the Lord of the Will to give and give (me all this, it would still be little).
O Nanak, the one on whom he casts his glance of grace has glory through the True Name.
147.2: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The mouth has never had its fill of speaking, nor the ears of hearing.
The eyes have never had their fill of seeing; (each sense) is a buyer of one kind of quality alone.
The hunger of the hungry does not leave them; hunger is not ended by talk.
O Nanak, the hungry one is sated only when, uttering (the Lord's) virtues, he merges in the Virtuous One.
147.3: Without the True One, all is false; only falsehood is earned.
Without the True One, the dealer in falsehood is tied up and led away.
Without the True One, the body is ash, and to ash it returns.
Without the True One, all that one wears and eats only (feeds) hunger.
Without the True One, through falsehood, (his) court is not reached.
Clinging to false greed, one loses (the Lord's) mansion.
The whole world has been cheated by the cheat (falsehood); (so) one comes and goes.
The fire of craving in the body is put out through the Shabad.
147.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the Guru is the tree of contentment; dharma is its blossom, and divine knowledge its fruit.
Full of the sap (of love), it stays ever green; through (God's) grace and meditation (its fruit) ripens.
One who eats (it) tastes the delights of (union with) the Husband (Lord); (this) is the gift above all gifts.
147.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(The Guru is) a golden tree: its leaves are coral, its flowers jewels and rubies;
on it grow fruits of gems, the words spoken by (his) mouth; in his heart of hearts he is in bliss.
O Nanak, (the one) on whom there is (God's) grace, and on whose face and forehead (such) destiny is written:
(for that one) the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are in the Guru's feet, and he worships them ever as the highest.
Cruelty, attachment, greed and anger: all four are streams of fire.
(Those who) fall in burn, O Nanak; by (God's) grace, clinging (to the Guru's feet), one crosses over.
147.6: Die while you are alive; killing (craving) so, one has no regrets (at the end).
False is this world; only a rare one has grasped (it).
(Man) does not set his love on the True One, and runs after worldly affairs.
(Yet) cruel death, death the destroyer, hangs over the head of the world.
By (the Lord's) Hukam, Jandar (the brute, Death's messenger) stands over (each) head, and strikes when his chance comes.
(God) himself gives (his) love, and (then) it is enshrined in the mind.
Not a moment, not an instant's delay (is allowed) when (life's) measure is full.
By the Guru's grace, understanding (this), one merges in the True One.
147.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The bitter gourd and the colocynth, poison, the swallow-wort, the thorn-apple and the neem fruit:
(O Lord,) these (bitter things) dwell in the mind and in the mouth of the one into whose thoughts you do not come.
O Nanak, to whom can (their state) be told? Bereft of (God's) grace, they wander about.
147.8: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The intellect is a bird; with its past deeds (kirat) beside it, it is now high, now low.
Now it perches on the sandalwood tree, now on a branch of the swallow-wort, and now (there is in it) a lofty love (for God).
O Nanak, (all) are made to move by (his) Hukam; this has been the Master's way (from the first).
148.1: Countless people give their accounts (of God), and having told and told, they depart.
The Vedas give their expositions, (yet) his limit cannot be found.
By reading, his secret is not found; it is found when understanding dawns.
Through the garb of the six orders (khat darshan), who has merged in the True One?
The True Being is beyond seeing; through the Shabad he becomes lovely (to the mind).
The one who has faith in the Name of the Countless One reaches (his) court.
He bows to the Creator, and as a minstrel he sings (his praise).
O Nanak, he enshrines in his mind the One who is in every age.
148.2: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
One who knows only the charm for scorpions, yet goes and lays hold of snakes,
sets a firebrand to himself with his own hands.
The Master's Hukam has gone forth from the very first: through overreaching, one is struck down.
The manmukh who sets himself against the Gurmukh drowns by (the Lord's) true justice.
Over both sides the Master himself (stands); he watches and judges between them.
O Nanak, know it so: everything is (done) in his Will.
148.3: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
O Nanak, if one assays oneself, then know (that one) to be an assayer.
One who knows both the illness and its remedy is a wise physician.
Such a one starts no quarrels on the road (of life), knowing himself a guest (here).
He speaks knowing the Root (of all), and brings harm upon what harms (him, the vices).
One who does not walk by greed and abides in the Truth: that go-between is accepted.
(If someone) aims an arrow at the sky, how can the shaft reach (it)?
It lies beyond, out of reach; know that (the arrow falls back on) the archer.
148.4: The soul-brides who love their Husband are adorned with love.
They worship day and night, and do not stop, though held back.
Made beautiful by the Shabad, they dwell in the (Lord's) mansion.
Thoughtful, they offer a true prayer.
Having come by his Hukam, they look beautiful beside the Master.
As his companions they make their prayer, loving (him) with all their heart.
Without the Name, cursed is the dwelling (in the world), and shame on such a life.
She whom he has adorned through the Shabad has drunk the Amrit (of the Name).
148.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The desert is never sated by rain, and the hunger of fire never leaves it.
No king was ever sated by his kingdom; and who has ever filled up the oceans?
O Nanak, what need to ask how great the longing for the True Name is? (It never ends.)
148.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Fruitless is the birth of that one, so long as he does not know Brahm (God).
By the Guru's grace many cross over the ocean of the world.
(God) is the Cause of creation, all-powerful: says Nanak, after reflection,
the cause (of all) is in the power of the Creator, who has established his power (in all creation).
148.7: The minstrel has come to dwell at the Master's court.
Praising the True Master, the lotus (of his heart) has blossomed.
Receiving the full (station) from the Master, he is glad at heart.
He has struck down and driven out his foes (the vices), and his friends rejoice.
Those who serve the True Guru: (he) has shown them the true path.
Reflecting on the true Shabad, they have destroyed (the fear of) death.
Made beautiful by the Shabad, the minstrel tells of the One beyond telling.
O Nanak, gathering the capital of virtues, he has met the beloved Lord.
149.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Born of wrongs, they commit wrongs, and so they sink (ever deeper) into wrongs.
These do not come off at all with washing, though they try a hundred washings.
O Nanak, if (God) pardons, they are pardoned; otherwise they are beaten with shoes.
149.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, it is idle prattle to ask for comforts and leave out pains.
Comfort and pain are both robes (given) at (the Lord's) door, which human beings come (into the world) and wear.
Where speaking only ends in defeat, there silence is best.
149.3: Having looked in all four directions, I searched my own self within,
(and saw that) the True Being, the Unseen, has created (the world) and watches over it.
To one lost in the wilderness, the Guru showed the way.
Wonderful is the True Guru, the true one, (through whom) the True One is cherished (in the heart).
The jewel (of the Name) was found within the house itself, (when the Guru) lit the lamp (of wisdom).
Those who hold to the Truth praise (God) through the true Shabad and are at peace.
Those without fear (of God) are seized by fear; they waste away in their pride.
Strayed from the Name, the world wanders about out of step.
149.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(The world) is born in fear and dies in fear, and fear stays ever in its mind.
O Nanak, whoever dies in the fear (of God): that one's coming (into the world) is blessed.
149.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One may live long, very long, without the fear (of God), and enjoy pleasure upon pleasure;
(yet) O Nanak, if one dies without the fear (of God), one rises and departs with a blackened face.
149.6: When the True Guru is merciful, faith is made whole.
When the True Guru is merciful, one never grieves.
When the True Guru is merciful, pain is not known at all.
When the True Guru is merciful, the Lord's love is enjoyed.
When the True Guru is merciful, what fear of Jam can there be?
When the True Guru is merciful, the body is at peace for ever.
When the True Guru is merciful, one finds the nine treasures.
When the True Guru is merciful, one merges in the True One.
149.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
They have the hair of their heads plucked out, drink dirty water, and beg and eat others' leavings.
They stir their excrement and breathe its stench, and shrink at the sight of water.
Like sheep, they have their heads plucked, and the hands (that pluck them) are filled with ash.
They throw away the work of their mothers and fathers (earning a living), and their families wail aloud.
For them there is no pind, no pattal, no kiria, no lamp; once dead, who knows where they are cast?
The sixty-eight tiraths give them no shelter, and Brahmins do not eat their food.
Day and night they stay ever unclean, with no tikka on the brow.
They sit with heads ever bowed, as if mourning a death, and go to no gathering or assembly.
Bowls hang at their waists and whisks are in their hands, and they walk in single file.
They are neither yogis nor jangams, neither qazis nor mullas.
Ruined by God, they wander in disgrace, and the whole flock roams accursed.
He alone kills living beings and brings them to life; no one else can protect (them).
They are cut off from giving and from bathing; ashes fall on their plucked heads.
It was from water that the jewels came forth, when Meru was made the churning stick.
The gods set up the sixty-eight tiraths (by the waters), where the holy days draw crowds and the sacred word is recited.
Having bathed, one says the namaz; having bathed, one worships; the wise bathe always.
In death and in life, one is made clean when water is poured over the head.
O Nanak, these hair-plucked ones are perverse (shaitani); the matter (of bathing) does not please them.
When the rain falls there is gladness; the very life of all beings rests in it.
When the rain falls, grain, sugarcane and cotton (grow), and cotton covers everyone.
When the rain falls, the cows graze on grass every day, and the woman (of the house) churns the curd.
With that ghee the hom, the yagya and worship are ever performed; with it added, every rite is graced.
The Guru is the ocean, and his teaching all the rivers: bathing in it, one gains glory.
O Nanak, if the hair-plucked ones do not bathe (in it), then seven handfuls of ash (fall) on their heads.
150.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
What can cold do to fire? What can night do to the sun?
What can darkness do to the moon? What can caste do to air and water?
What can things do to the earth, in which everything comes to be?
O Nanak, honour is known (as true) only when he himself keeps (one's) honour.
150.2: O True One, I have ever praised you as Subhan (the Wondrous).
You are the true Ruler (Diwan); all others come and go.
Those who ask (of you) the gift of Truth become like you.
True is your command; through the Shabad it is beautiful (to them).
By obeying (your command), wisdom and meditation are received from you.
By (your) grace the mark (of approval) is set, which no one can remove.
You are the true Giver; you give every day, and ever more and more.
Nanak begs for the gift that pleases you.
150.3: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Those whom (the Guru) has given understanding by imparting his teaching, and merged in the True One through praise:
what (further) teaching can be given to those whose Guru is Nanak Dev?
150.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Only the one whom he himself gives understanding understands.
The one to whom he himself gives sight sees everything.
One who talks and talks in discourse only wrangles over Maya.
By his Hukam he makes all forms.
He himself knows what is in the thoughts of all.
O Nanak, the Word is his own utterance.
The doubt of the one who receives (this) gift is removed.
150.5: I was a minstrel with no work; (the Lord) set me to (his) work.
From the very first he commanded: Night or day, sing (my) vaar (of praise).
The Master called the minstrel into his true mansion.
He robed (me) in the robe of honour of his true praise.
The true, ambrosial Name came to (me) as food.
Whoever, by the Guru's teaching, has eaten (of it) to the full has found peace.
The minstrel shares (this) blessing (with all), and has made the Shabad resound.
Praising the True One, Nanak has found the Perfect (Lord).
151.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade and Dupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
The fear of God is very heavy; its weight is great.
The mind's own counsel is light, and (one who follows it) speaks light words.
If one walks with (this fear) set upon the head and bears its weight,
then, by (God's) glance of grace and his favour, the Guru's wisdom is gained.
No one crosses (the world-ocean) without the fear (of God).
(Only they cross who,) living in that fear and adorning (their lives) with love, have kept the fear (in the heart).
In the fear (of God) the fire within the body blazes, and with that fear it keeps ablaze;
in the fear, and adorned through the Shabad, a life of reverent fear is fashioned.
Without the fear, what is fashioned is raw, utterly raw:
the mould is blind, and blind is the hammer's stroke.
In (the self-willed one's) intellect arises a craving for the play (of the world);
for all its thousand clevernesses, the heat (of the fear) does not reach it.
O Nanak, the speech of the manmukh is (empty as) the wind;
his word is blind, idle wind and worthless.
151.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Through the fear (of God) one finds the home (within), and in that home dwells the fear; through that fear, (every other) fear departs.
What sort of fear is that, if in it some (other) fear still takes hold?
(O Lord,) apart from you there is no other place (of refuge);
whatever happens is all your will.
One would be afraid if there were some other to fear;
to live in fear upon fear is only the turmoil of the mind.
The soul does not die, nor does it drown or swim across.
He who made (all) this does everything.
By his Hukam one comes, and by his Hukam one goes;
in this world and the next, one abides within his Hukam.
Where there is cruelty, attachment, desire and pride,
there hunger (craving) runs high, like a river (in flood).
The fear (of God) is (the soul's) food and drink, its support;
without eating it, the foolish waste away and die.
Rare, very rare, is the one who has someone (to call his own);
everyone is yours, and you are the one who cares for all.
He to whom belong all beings and creatures, all wealth and property:
O Nanak, to describe him and to reflect on him is hard.
151.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Make wisdom your mother and contentment your father,
and make truthful living your special brother.
There is something to say, but it cannot be said:
(O Lord,) the worth of your creation cannot be reckoned.
Effort and awareness, these two, have become the parents-in-law,
and, O mind, good conduct has been taken as the wife.
Union (with the holy) is the wedding day, and parting (from the world) the marriage;
truth is the offspring: says Nanak, this is the union (with God).
152.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(The body) is a union of air, water and fire,
the play of a restless, fickle intellect.
(It has) nine doors, and the Tenth Gate:
O wise one, understand this thought.
He (the Lord) alone is the one who speaks, utters and hears.
The one who reflects on his own self becomes truly wise.
The body is clay; it is the air (the breath) that speaks.
O wise one, understand: who is it that has died?
What has died is the awareness (that ran after Maya), strife and pride;
the One who beholds (all) has not died.
That for which (people) go to the banks of tiraths,
that jewel, that treasure, is within the heart itself.
Reading and reading, the pandit voices his arguments,
but does not know the thing that is within (him).
I have not died; what has died is my demon (of mine-ness).
The One who pervades all has not died.
Says Nanak, the Guru has shown me Brahm (God),
and (now) I see no one dying or being born.
152.2: Raag Gauri Dakhani, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The one who, hearing again and again, understands and accepts the Name,
to him I am ever a sacrifice.
Those whom (the Lord) himself leads astray find no place, no refuge;
(O Lord,) you give understanding, and join (us) in union (with you).
May I receive the Naam, that it may go with me;
without the Name, all are bound by death.
The support of the Name is (my) farming and (my) trade;
sin and merit are a bundle of seed (that will sprout).
Those within whose hearts lust and anger strike their blows
forget the Name and depart with falseness in their minds.
True is the teaching of the True Guru:
(by it) body and mind are cooled, and the True One is recognised.
The mark (of those who receive it) is that they live untouched, like the water-lily and the lotus in water;
steeped in the Shabad, they are sweet as the juice of the sugarcane.
By (his) Hukam, through the joining (of destiny), the fortress (of the body) with ten gates (is made);
in it the five (elements) dwell, joined with the infinite Light.
He is himself the goods that are weighed, and himself the trader;
O Nanak, through the Name he is the one who adorns (all).
152.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
How can it be known where (the soul) comes from,
where it springs from, and where it goes and merges?
How is it bound, and how does it win liberation?
How does it merge in the imperishable (state of) Sahaj?
One who has the Naam in the heart and the ambrosial Name on the lips
through the Name of the Lord (Narhar) becomes, like the Lord, free of desire.
(The soul) comes of itself, by the natural order, and of itself it goes;
it springs from the mind and merges into the mind.
The Gurmukh is free; no bond holds him.
Reflecting on the Shabad, he is released through the Lord's Name.
On a tree many birds make their home for the night;
some happy, some sad, they are ruined by attachment in the mind.
As evening passes into dawn, they look to the sky,
and fly off in the ten directions; (so beings) run about as their deeds have written.
Those joined to the Name (take this world as) a brief halt in a goil (a pasture);
(in them) the poisoned pot of lust and anger bursts.
Without the goods (of the Name), house and shop (of the heart) lie empty;
meeting the Guru, the hard shutters are opened.
The Saadh (the holy Guru) is met through destiny from the past;
the perfect people of the Lord rejoice in the True One.
Giving their minds and bodies, they receive (the Name) in Sahaj and with love;
Nanak touches their feet.
153.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(In me are) lust and anger, and my mind is in Maya;
my mind's love wakes to falsehood and vice;
I have gathered a capital of sin and greed.
(O Lord, your) purifying Name in the mind is the raft and the boat (to cross over).
Wonderful, wonderful are you, O True One; I lean on you (alone).
I am a sinner; you alone are pure.
Like water set on the fire, (the mortal) seethes and bubbles in his speech;
the tongue and each sense has its own craving;
the gaze is on vice; there is neither fear nor love (of God).
Only by killing self-conceit does one obtain the Name.
One who dies through the Shabad does not die again;
without dying (so), how can one become perfect?
The mind stays caught in the world's show and in duality;
Narayan is eternal: whatever he does, that comes to pass.
I can board the ship (of the Name) only when my turn comes;
those held back from the ship are beaten in the Lord's court.
I praise the True One; blessed is the Guru's door.
O Nanak, at (the Guru's) door and in the home (of the heart) is the One Creator, Ekankar.
153.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Reflecting on God (Brahm), the (inverted) lotus (of the heart) has turned upright;
in the sky of the Tenth Gate the stream of Amrit flows;
the Lord (Murari) himself pervades the three worlds.
O my mind, do not wander in doubt;
when the mind is won over, the essence of Amrit is drunk.
Having won (the game of) life, the mind has accepted death (to self);
self-conceit has died, and the mind has come to know (this) from within itself;
(the Lord's) glance of grace has fallen, and within one's own home the home (of the Lord) is known.
Continence, truthful living, pilgrimage and holy bathing lie in the Name;
why should I make a great show (of anything else)?
The Lord, Nar Narayan, knows every heart from within.
Were I to believe in any other, only then would I go to another's house;
of whom should I ask? There is no other place.
Through the Guru's teaching, Nanak is absorbed in Sahaj.
153.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If the True Guru is met, he shows (one) that death (to self)
whose joy, the joy of dying (so) and (truly) living, becomes dear within;
casting off pride, one reaches the city in the sky (the highest state of the spirit).
(All) have come with death written (for them); no one is to stay (here).
By repeating and meditating on the Lord, one finds a lasting abode in the Lord's refuge.
If the True Guru is met, duality runs away;
the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, and the mind clings to the Lord God;
one who dies while living has the supreme joy before him.
When the True Guru is met, one becomes pure through the discipline of truth;
(climbing) the Guru's ladder, one rises higher and higher;
by (God's) grace (this) is found, and the fear of Jam comes to an end.
When the Guru is met, one meets (the Lord) and merges in his embrace;
in his grace (the Guru) has shown (him) the home, the mansion (of the Lord);
O Nanak, (the Guru) has killed his Haumai and united him (with the Lord).
154.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What has fallen (to one's lot) from past deeds, no one can erase;
what can I know of what lies ahead?
Whatever pleased him is what has come to pass;
there is no second, no other, who does anything.
(O Lord,) I do not know how great your grace is, how great your gift;
your Name is my deeds, my dharma and my caste.
You are so great a Giver, the One who gives to all;
your storehouses of devotion never run short.
The pride one takes is of no avail;
soul and body, all is in your keeping.
You slay and bring to life again; forgiving, you unite (with yourself);
as it pleases you, so you have (beings) repeat your Name.
You are the Knower, the Seer, the True One over my head;
(you) give the Guru's teaching; I rest my trust in you.
No filth remains in the body of one whose mind is dyed (in your love);
through the Guru's words, through the Shabad, he has recognised the True One.
Your strength is (his support), and the glory of your Name (his honour);
O Nanak, (he) dwells in devotion, in (the Lord's) refuge.
154.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who speaks of the Unspeakable and has others speak of him, who drinks the nectar (of the Name) and gives it to others to drink,
forgets every other fear and is absorbed in the Name.
Why should such a one fear? (All his) fear has merged in the fear (of God),
(for he) has come to know (the Lord) through the Shabad of the Perfect Guru.
The one in whose heart the Lord dwells, whose capital is the Lord (Hari),
abiding in Sahaj and in love, receives (the Lord's) approval.
Those whom (the Lord) keeps asleep (in Maya) evening and morning,
those manmukhs are bound by death, here and hereafter.
Those with the Lord in their hearts day and night are perfect;
O Nanak, meeting the Lord, they are rid of their doubts.
154.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who loves (Maya of) the three qualities is born and dies (again and again);
the four Vedas tell (only) of the visible form;
they expound the three states;
(but) the fourth state is (union with) the Lord: know him through the True Guru.
Through devotion to the Lord and service of the Guru one swims across (the world-ocean);
(then) there is no birth again, and no death.
Everyone talks of the four great gifts;
the Simritis, the Shastras and the pandits have the same on their lips;
(but) without the Guru, (their true) meaning and understanding are not found;
the gift of liberation is found through devotion to the Lord.
The one in whose heart that Lord has come to dwell
has received devotion through the Guru.
In devotion to the Lord is the bliss of liberation;
through the Guru's teaching one finds supreme bliss.
Whoever has found (this bliss), the Guru, having seen (the Lord himself), has shown (him) to that one,
and has taught him to stay free of hopes while living amid hopes.
(That Lord) is the Master of the lowly, the Giver of every comfort;
O Nanak, (that one's) mind stays dyed in (love of) the Lord's feet.
154.4: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The body, (thinking itself) immortal, lives at its ease; (but) this world is (only) a play.
(O body,) you practise greed, avarice and much falsehood, and carry a great load (of sin).
O body, I have seen you scattered like ashes over the ground.
(O soul,) listen, listen to my counsel:
only the good you have done will stay (with you), my soul; this turn will not come again.
I tell you, O my body, listen to my counsel:
you brood on slander of others and carry false tales;
you cast your eyes on another's wife, O soul, and you steal and do evil.
When the swan (the soul) departs, you (O body) will be left behind, like a deserted wife.
O body, you have lived as if in a dream; what deeds have you done?
When I stole and brought something home, it seemed good to (your) mind;
(so) there is no honour here and no shelter hereafter; the precious (human) life is wasted.
(The body says:) I have become most wretched, O brother; O Nanak, no one asks after me now.
Horses of Arab and Turki breed, gold and silver, loads of fine clothes:
(none of them) has gone along with anyone, O Nanak; they have dropped away (and stayed here), you fool.
Rock sugar and dried fruits, I have tasted everything; your Name alone is Amrit.
Laying foundation upon foundation, the walls are raised, (but those) mansions (become) a heap of ashes;
(one) piles up hoards and gives nothing to anyone; the blind one thinks it is all his own.
Lanka of gold, palaces of gold (did not last): wealth stays with no one.
Listen, foolish and ignorant mind:
his will alone shall prevail.
Our Master is the great Banker, and we are his traders;
soul and body, all of it, is his capital; he himself slays and he himself brings to life.
155.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The others (the foes: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) are five, and I am one alone; how can I guard my house and home, O mind?
Day after day they beat and rob (me); before whom can I cry out, O brother?
O mind, utter the Name of Sri Ram (the Lord);
ahead of you stands the army of Jam, vast and terrible.
(God) built the hut (of the body) and set doors in it, and within it sits the soul-bride;
(thinking herself) immortal, the bride revels every day in her pleasures, while those other five go on robbing (her).
(Jam's army) pulled down the hut and plundered the temple, and the bride was seized, all alone;
Jam's club (struck), the chain fell about her neck, and those five ran away.
A wife craves gold and silver; friends crave things to eat;
O Nanak, for their sake (a man) commits sins, and will go bound to the city of Jam.
155.2: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O yogi,) the (true) earrings are those within the heart; make the body itself your patched coat;
bring the five disciples (the senses) under control, O Raval, and make this mind your staff.
In this way you will find the way of Yoga:
there is one Shabad, and no other; set your mind on that (as your food of) roots and tubers.
If by shaving the head the Guru is found, we have made the Guru our Ganga;
you do not remember the one Lord, the Saviour of the three worlds, O blind one.
Making a show, you win (people's) minds with (mere) talk; your (own) doubt does not leave you at all.
If you fix your consciousness on the feet of the One, why would you chase after greed and avarice?
With your mind absorbed (in him), repeat (the Name of) the Niranjan;
why, O yogi, do you speak so much deceit?
The body is crazed and the swan (the soul) a child; life goes by in crying, mine, mine.
Nanak humbly prays: when the naked (body) burns, then, afterwards, (the soul) repents.
156.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O mind, the One alone is the root of all medicine and every mantra, if you make your consciousness firm (in him);
take (the Name of) the One who cuts away the sinful deeds of birth after birth.
O brother, the Master of the mind is the One alone;
(while) your three qualities stay engrossed in the world, the Unseen cannot be perceived.
Maya tastes sweet to the body, like sugar; we have taken up (its) bundle;
the night is dark and nothing can be seen, and the mouse (of time) gnaws away at the rope (of life), O brother.
As much as the manmukhs act (by their own will), so much pain befalls them; the Gurmukh receives honour.
What he has done, that alone has come to be; the record of past deeds cannot be erased.
Those who are dyed (in the Lord), having given (him) their love, are full to the brim and never run dry;
if Nanak becomes the dust of their feet, then (this) fool too may gain something.
156.2: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Since when has (anyone) been our mother, since when our father? From what place have we come?
We took shape in the fire (of the womb), from the water (of the seed): for what purpose were we made?
O my Master, who knows your virtues?
How many lives as trees and plants we have seen; how many times we were made beasts;
how many times we came among the families of snakes; how many times we were made to fly as birds.
(Man) breaks into the town's shops and its solid houses, and having stolen, comes home;
he looks ahead and looks behind, (but) where can he hide from you, (O Lord)?
We have seen river banks and tiraths, the nine regions (of the earth), shops, towns and bazaars;
(at last) the trader took up the scales and began to weigh within his own heart.
As full as the ocean is of water, so many are our faults.
Show mercy, show some kindness: you have carried sinking stones across.
The soul burns like fire; a knife (of craving) cuts within;
Nanak humbly prays: (one who) recognises the Hukam has peace day and night.
156.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
You have wasted the night in sleep and the day in eating;
this life is (precious) as a diamond, yet it goes in exchange for a cowrie shell.
You have not known the Name of the Lord;
(Man) buries endless wealth in the earth, (but) the Endless One is not longed for;
those who went off longing for endless (wealth) came back having lost the Endless One.
If it came to whoever reached out and took it, everyone would be rich;
it is settled by deeds, however much everyone may long (for it).
O Nanak, the One who made the creation takes care of it;
no one can tell the Master's Hukam, to whom he will give glory.
157.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Were I a doe, I would live in the forest, picking roots and tubers to eat,
and if by the Guru's grace my Husband (the Lord) met me, I would give myself up to him again and again.
(O Lord,) your Name is my merchandise and my trade.
Were I a koel (the Indian cuckoo), I would dwell in the mango tree and reflect on the Shabad in Sahaj;
in Sahaj and in love my Husband would meet me, whose sight and form are beyond all measure.
Were I a fish, I would live in the water (of the Lord), who takes care of all beings and creatures;
my Husband dwells on this shore and on the far shore; I will meet him with my arms spread wide.
Were I a she-snake, I would dwell in the earth; (if) the Shabad dwelt (within me), fear would go.
O Nanak, they are ever happy soul-brides, whose light merges in the Light.
157.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi Deepaki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
In the house where (God's) praise is spoken and the Creator is reflected upon,
in that house sing the Sohila and remember the Creator.
Sing the Sohila of my Fearless Lord.
I am a sacrifice to the Sohila by which there is peace for ever.
Day after day all beings are cared for; the Giver will watch over (each one).
(O soul,) you cannot set a value on his giving; what measure can be taken of that Giver?
The year and the day (of my wedding) have been written; gather, (friends,) and pour the oil (of the wedding rite).
Give me your blessings, friends, so that I may be united with my Master.
To every house this same summons comes; these calls go out every day.
Let us remember the One who sends the call; O Nanak, those days are coming (for us too).
157.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
When the Guru is met, union with the Lord comes about;
that (Lord) himself brings (one) into his union.
My God himself knows every way;
by his Hukam he unites (one), who then recognises (him) through the Shabad.
In the fear of the True Guru, doubt and dread depart;
one steeped in that fear merges in the love of the True One.
When the Guru is met, the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, of his own loving nature.
My God is great; his worth cannot be found.
Whoever praises him through the Shabad, him who has no end and no near or far shore,
my God, the Forgiver, forgives (that one).
When the Guru is met, all wisdom and understanding come;
that True One dwells in the mind made pure.
When the True One dwells (within), all one's work is true;
reflection on the Shabad is the noblest conduct.
True service comes from the Guru;
through the Guru, some rare one recognises the Naam.
The Giver, who bestows all gifts, lives for ever;
O Nanak, (by his gift) love for the Lord's Name takes hold.
158.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Some rare one receives spiritual wisdom from the Guru;
the one who comes to understand from the Guru succeeds.
From the Guru come Sahaj and reflection on the True One;
from the Guru one finds the door of liberation.
By perfect fortune the Guru comes and meets one,
and one merges in true Sahaj, in the True One.
When the Guru is met, one quenches the fire of craving;
from the Guru, peace comes to dwell in the mind.
From the Guru come purity, holiness and cleanness;
from the Guru, union (with God) comes about through the Shabad.
Without the Guru, all (the world) is led astray in doubt;
without the Name, it suffers great pain.
One who becomes Gurmukh meditates on the Naam;
through the sight of the True One, true honour is gained.
To whom else should one speak? That One alone is the Giver;
when he shows grace, union comes about through the Shabad.
Having met the Beloved (Guru), may I sing the True One's praises;
may Nanak, becoming true, merge in the True One.
158.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
True is that place (the Sat Sangat), where the mind becomes pure;
one makes one's dwelling in the True One, and becomes true.
The true Bani is manifest through all four ages;
the True One is himself everything, of his own self.
When (God's) grace comes, he brings one into the Sat Sangat,
and, seated in that place, one sings the Lord's praises.
Let this tongue burn that is in the love of another,
that does not taste the Lord's sweet essence and utters insipid words.
Without understanding (that taste), body and mind become insipid;
without the Name, the wretched one departs weeping.
One whose tongue has tasted the Lord's sweet essence abides in Sahaj and in love;
by the Guru's grace, that one merges in the True One.
Dyed in the True One, (the tongue) makes the Guru's Shabad its reflection,
and (that one) drinks the pure stream of Amrit.
That which is a (fit) vessel merges in the Name;
in a vessel turned upside down (the heart turned away from God) nothing stays.
Through the Guru's Shabad the Name comes to dwell in the mind;
O Nanak, that vessel is true which thirsts for the Shabad.
158.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Some keep on singing, but their mind finds no relish;
they sing in Haumai, and it goes to waste.
They truly sing the songs (of praise) who love the Name;
(theirs is) the true Bani and reflection on the Shabad.
One keeps on singing (his praise) if it pleases the True Guru;
mind and body dyed in the Name, (one's life) becomes beautiful.
Some sing, and some perform worship (with dance and show),
but without love they do not obtain the Naam.
True devotion lies in love for the Guru's Shabad;
(such devotees) have kept their own Beloved ever enshrined in the heart.
Fools perform worship and make a show of themselves;
they dance and dance and leap about, and suffer much pain.
By dancing and leaping, devotion is not done;
the one who dies (to self) through the Shabad, that one obtains devotion.
He, the Lover of devotion, himself causes devotion to be done;
true devotion is to lose self-conceit from within.
My true God knows every way (of all);
O Nanak, the one he forgives recognises the Naam.
159.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When one subdues the mind, its wandering dies away;
without dying (to self), how can one find the Lord?
Rare is the one who knows the medicine by which the mind dies;
the mind dies through the Shabad: that one alone understands this.
The one whom he forgives, he grants the glory
that, by the Guru's grace, the Lord comes to dwell in the mind.
When, through the Guru, one practises the conduct worth practising,
then one comes to understand this mind.
The mind is drunk, like an elephant maddened by wine;
the Guru, striking it with the goad, brings it to life.
The mind is hard to tame; some rare one tames it.
When one consumes what will not yield (the mind's stubbornness), then (the mind) becomes pure.
Through the Guru, one has set this mind in order,
and casts Haumai and the vices out from within.
Those whom he has, from the very beginning, kept joined in his union
are never parted (from him); they stay merged in the Shabad.
He himself alone knows his own power;
O Nanak, through the Guru one recognises the Naam.
159.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Haumai the whole world has gone mad;
in the love of another, it has strayed, lost in doubt.
It frets with many anxious thoughts, but has not known its own self;
busy with worldly affairs, its every day has slipped away.
Remember the Lord (Ram) in your heart, O my brother;
through the Guru, let your tongue savour the Lord's sweet essence.
One who, through the Guru, has recognised the Lord in the heart,
serving the Life of the world, is known through the four ages.
Killing Haumai, one recognises (him) through the Guru's Shabad,
when God, the Ordainer of destinies, shows his grace.
True are those people whom he joins to the Guru's Shabad;
he checks their running (mind) and holds it still.
They obtain from the Guru the Naam, the nine treasures;
through the Lord's grace, the Lord comes to abide in their minds.
Repeating Ram, Ram, the body finds peace and calm;
when he dwells within, the pain of Jam does not touch one.
He himself is the Master, and he himself the minister;
O Nanak, serve for ever the Lord, the deep ocean of virtues.
159.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Why should he be forgotten, to whom belong our soul and breath?
Why should he be forgotten who pervades all,
by serving whom one is honoured and accepted in the Lord's court?
I give myself in sacrifice to the Lord's Name;
if I forget you, that very moment I die.
They forget you whom you yourself have led astray;
they forget you who are in the love of another.
The ignorant manmukhs are cast into births.
Those with whom (the Lord) is wholly pleased, he sets to the True Guru's service;
those with whom he is wholly pleased, in their minds the Lord makes (himself) dwell.
Following the Guru's teaching, they merge in the Lord's Name.
Those who have merit in their store reflect on divine wisdom;
those who have merit in their store have killed Haumai.
Nanak is a sacrifice to those who are dyed in the Name.
160.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
You are beyond telling; how can you be told?
With the Guru's Shabad as the means that kills (the mind's ego), you come to dwell in the mind.
Your virtues are countless; their worth cannot be found.
The Bani (of praise) merges in the One to whom it belongs;
your untold story the Guru's Shabad has proclaimed.
Where the True Guru is, there the Sat Sangat is formed;
where the True Guru is, the Lord's praises are sung in Sahaj;
where the True Guru is, there the Shabad burns Haumai away.
Through the Guru, by service one finds a place in (the Lord's) mansion;
through the Guru, one enshrines the Lord's Name within;
through the Guru, by devotion one merges in the Lord's Name.
The Giver himself bestows the gift,
(and that one's) love for the perfect True Guru takes hold.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Name are hailed in glory.
160.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
From the One come all forms and colours;
air, water and fire: all of them are joined together (in every being).
The Lord God watches over (his creation of) many different colours.
This is a wonder: he alone is the One (in all);
rare is the one who, through the Guru, reflects on this.
In Sahaj, God pervades every place;
somewhere hidden, somewhere manifest: God has fashioned this design.
He himself awakens those who sleep.
His worth has never been found by anyone;
everyone speaks and speaks, describing him.
One who merges in the Guru's Shabad comes to understand that Lord.
Hearing (all) again and again, he watches over them and joins (them) to the Shabad;
great glory is gained through service of the Guru.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Name merge in the Lord's Name.
160.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh lies asleep in attachment to Maya, in love with her.
The Gurmukh stays awake, dwelling on the knowledge of (God's) virtues.
They alone are awake who are in love with the Naam.
In Sahaj such a one stays awake and never falls asleep (in attachment),
whoever comes to understand through the perfect Guru.
The unsaintly one, set in his stubborn ways, never understands.
He talks (of wisdom), yet stays entangled, struggling with Maya.
The blind, ignorant one never succeeds.
In this age, deliverance comes through the Name of Ram.
Some rare one gains this understanding through the Guru's Shabad.
He crosses over himself, and saves all his family lines as well.
In this Kalyug no ritual or religious observance (avails).
Kalyug is born in the house of the chandal.
O Nanak, without the Name no one is liberated.
161.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
True is (his) command; true is the King.
Those whose minds are dyed in the True One, the Lord who needs no one,
dwell in the True One's mansion and merge in the True Name.
Listen, my mind: reflect on the Shabad.
Repeat (the Name of) Ram, and cross over the ocean of the world.
In doubt one comes, and in doubt one goes;
this world is born in the love of another (than God).
The manmukh does not remember (the Lord), and keeps coming and going.
Has (this being) strayed of itself, or has God himself led it astray?
This soul has been set to serve what is not its own;
it earns great pain, and wastes its life in vain.
When (God), in his grace, brings (one) to the True Guru,
that one remembers the one Name, and does away with doubt from within.
O Nanak, such a one repeats the Naam, and obtains the Name, which is (to him) the nine treasures.
161.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
I go and ask those who have meditated (on the Lord) through the Guru;
by serving the Guru the mind is won over.
They are the wealthy who earn the Lord's Name;
this understanding is gained from the perfect Guru.
O my brothers, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
The labour of service done through the Guru, the Lord accepts.
One who recognises his own self, his mind becomes pure;
he is liberated while yet alive, and finds the Lord.
One who sings the Lord's praises, his understanding becomes sublime,
and with ease he merges in Sahaj.
In the love of another, (the Lord) cannot be served;
(such a one) eats the deadly poison of Haumai and Maya.
Through son, family and home, Maya has bewitched (him);
the blind manmukh keeps coming and going.
The one to whom (the Lord) gives the Name of the Lord, Har Har, is (his) servant;
through the Guru's Shabad his devotion goes on night and day.
Through the Guru's teaching some rare one understands (this);
O Nanak, that one merges in the Naam.
161.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Service of the Guru has held good in all four ages;
some perfect person carries out this task.
Inexhaustible is the wealth of the Lord's Name; there is never any shortage in it.
(With it) there is lasting peace here, and glory at (the Lord's) door.
O my mind, have no doubt (of this);
by service through the Guru, drink the essence of Amrit.
Those who serve the True Guru are the great beings of the world;
they are saved themselves, and carry all their family lines across.
They keep the Lord's Name enshrined in the heart;
dyed in the Naam, they cross the terrifying world-ocean.
Those who serve the True Guru are ever servants at heart;
The Anhad (Shabad) plays (within them), and they dwell in their own home;
dyed in the Naam, they stay detached while living in the home.
Those who serve the True Guru, their word is true (and lasting);
in every age the devotees have uttered it and made it known.
Night and day they repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Saringpani.
O Nanak, dyed in the Naam, they become pure and free of desire.
162.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(The one who) meets the True Guru by great fortune and by destiny's union
has the Naam in (his) heart, and ever enjoys the Lord's sweet essence.
The mortal who meditates on the Lord's Name through the Guru
wins this human life, and gains the profit of the Naam.
The Guru's Shabad is wisdom and meditation (to one who finds it) sweet;
(but) by the Guru's grace some rare one alone has tasted (it) and seen.
(People) carry out many rites and ceremonies and religious observances;
without the Name, cursed, cursed is (such) pride.
Tied in bonds, (the mortal is caught) in Maya's noose;
O servant Nanak, he is set free (only) by the light the Guru gives.
162.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
As the cloud rains down upon the earth, is there not water within the earth (as well)?
Just as water comes forth within the earth, (so the same water) the footless (clouds) go about raining.
O brother, in this way dispel (your) doubt:
as (the Lord) makes anyone, so that one becomes, and that is the way beings go and are absorbed.
Born woman or man, what deeds can they do (of themselves)?
(O Lord,) the many forms are ever yours, and they merge in you alone.
Through so many births (beings) lay astray; when (you) were found, they strayed no more.
He whose work (the world) is, he alone knows it well; (this is seen) if (beings) merge in the Guru's Shabad.
(O Lord,) yours is the Shabad, your command; you alone are (all) yourself; where then is doubt?
O Nanak, (those whose) essence has merged with the Essence do not come into birth again and again.
162.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The whole world is in the power of death, bound by the love of another.
Doing their deeds in Haumai, the manmukhs receive punishment.
O my mind, fix your attention on the Guru's feet.
Through the Guru take the treasure of the Naam; it will set (you) free in the Lord's court.
(Beings) wander through the eighty-four lakh (forms of life); by the mind's stubbornness one comes and goes.
(One who) has not recognised the Guru's Shabad falls into wombs again and again.
One who has recognised his own self through the Guru, the Lord's Name has come to dwell in his mind.
Dyed in devotion night and day, he stays merged in peace in the Lord's Name.
When the mind dies through the Shabad, faith takes root, and one gives up Haumai and the vices.
O servant Nanak, the treasures of the Lord's Name and of devotion are obtained only by (his) grace.
162.4: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the parents' home (this world) the stay is four days; so the Lord, Har Har, has written it.
Honoured is the (soul-) bride who has sung (his) praises through the Guru.
(She who) gathers virtues in her parents' home finds a dwelling in her in-laws' home (the world hereafter).
Through the Guru she stays merged in Sahaj, and the Lord, Har Har, is dear to her mind.
The Husband dwells in the in-laws' home and in the parents' home; say, by what means is he found?
He himself is stainless and beyond knowing; he himself unites (one with himself).
You, God, yourself give the understanding, (and then) the Lord's Name is meditated on.
By great fortune the True Guru is met, and Amrit is put into the mouth.
Haumai and duality perish, and with ease one merges in peace.
He himself, himself alone, pervades all; he himself attaches (one) to the Name.
The manmukhs, in their pride, have not found (him); they are ignorant and childish.
They do not serve the True Guru, and they repent again and again.
