O Nanak, by repeating the Naam they are saved, and at the True One's door they are acclaimed.
218.3: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O my soul, sing the Lord's sweet virtues; sing the Lord's sweet virtues.
Imbued with the True One, even one without a place has found a place.
All other tastes are insipid; (through them) body and mind become insipid;
whatever one does without the Supreme God, a curse on that life.
Holding the hem of the Saadh (the Guru), this world (-ocean) is crossed.
When the Supreme Lord is worshipped, the whole family is saved.
He alone is companion, kinsman and good friend who gives the Lord's Name (to keep) in the heart;
who wipes out all faults and does good (to others).
The Lord's feet are the treasures: (they are my) wealth, treasury, dwelling and home.
O God, Nanak is a beggar at your door; he begs for you as his gift.
219.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O holy ones, give up the pride of the mind.
Lust and anger are the company of the wicked: flee from it day and night.
(One who) holds pleasure and pain both as alike, and honour and dishonour too;
who stays aloof from joy and grief: he has recognised the essence in the world.
(One who) gives up both praise and slander, and seeks the state of nirvana, where desire is stilled —
O servant Nanak, this is a hard game; only a rare one has come to know it through the Guru.
219.2: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O holy ones, Ram has made (such) a creation
that one perishes while another deems (himself) everlasting; this wonder cannot be described.
In the grip of lust, anger and attachment, the mortal has forgotten the Lord's being;
he has taken the false body to be true, like a dream in the night.
Everything that is seen perishes, as a cloud's shadow does.
O servant Nanak, (one who) has known the world to be false remains in Ram's refuge.
219.3: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
The Lord's praise does not enter the mortal's mind.
Day and night he stays absorbed in Maya; tell me, how can he sing (the Lord's) virtues?
With possessive love for sons, friends and Maya, in this way he binds himself;
this world is false like a mirage (the deer's thirst), yet seeing it he rises and runs after it.
The Master who is the source of (worldly) enjoyment and of liberation: the fool forgets him.
O servant Nanak, only one in millions is granted the devotion of Ram.
219.4: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O holy ones, this mind cannot be held in check.
It dwells with fickle craving; therefore it does not stay steady.
Harsh anger too is within the heart itself, and it has made all sense be forgotten;
it has stolen everyone's jewel of wisdom; against it no one has any power.
All the yogis have failed in their efforts; the learned have grown weary of singing praises.
O servant Nanak, when the Lord became kind, then every way came right.
219.5: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O holy ones, sing the praises of Gobind.
(You) have been given a priceless human birth; why waste it in vain?
The Lord purifies the fallen and is kin to the lowly; come into his refuge.
Remembering him, the terror of Gaj (the elephant) was ended; why do you forget him?
Giving up pride and the attachment of Maya, then fix your mind on Ram's worship.
Says Nanak: this is the path of liberation; become Gurmukh, and you will find it.
219.6: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mother, let someone counsel (this) strayed mind.
Though it hears the Vedas, the Puranas and the way of the holy, it does not sing the Lord's praises even for an instant.
Having gained the human body, so hard to obtain, it passes its life in vain.
The attachment of Maya is a forest of great peril, and (the mind) grows fond of that very thing.
God, who is ever with (it) within and without: with him it forms no love.
Says Nanak: know him alone to be liberated in whose heart Ram dwells.
220.1: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O holy ones, in Ram's refuge is rest.
This is the merit of reading the Vedas and Puranas: that one remembers the Lord's Name.
Greed, attachment, Maya, possessiveness and the indulging of the senses,
joy and grief: the one whom these do not touch is the very image of God.
Heaven and hell, nectar and poison, all these (are alike to him), and so are gold and a copper coin;
to whom praise and slander are the same, and greed and attachment likewise;
the one whom these, pain and pleasure, do not bind: know him to be a giani (one who truly knows).
Says Nanak: know that mortal to be liberated who lives in this way.
220.2: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mind, why have you gone mad?
Day and night the lifespan wears away, but (the mortal) does not know it; in greed's company he has become hollow.
The body you have taken as your own, and your fine house and wife:
none of these is yours, O (mind); reflect, consider and see.
You have gambled away your jewel of a life, and have not known the way of Gobind.
Not for an instant have you been absorbed in (his) feet; your life has run out in vain.
Says Nanak: that man alone is happy who sings the praises of Ram's Name;
the whole world besides is lured by Maya, and does not reach the fearless state.
220.3: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
The One who is merciful to the lowly and destroys all fears: fall into his refuge.
He whose praises the Vedas and Puranas sing: hold his Name in your heart.
The Lord's Name is the purifier in the world; remembering him again and again, wash away all sins.
You will not gain the human body again; make some effort for (your) liberation.
Says Nanak: sing (the praises of) the Lord who is all compassion, and cross over the world-ocean.
220.4: Raag Gauri Guareri, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace.
Reflection on the pure Naam is (for me) the treasures and the siddhis;
with the poison (of Maya) killed, (I see) the Perfect One filling all;
in the Pure (Name) the trikuti (the mind's fretting) is gone;
the Guru's counsel has proved of use within my soul.
In this way, dwelling on Ram, the mind has been won over;
through the Guru's Shabad I have recognised the collyrium of divine knowledge.
(The mind) has come to prize the one peace (of the Name), and (it) has joined me in Sahaj;
the pure Bani has ended doubt;
(with the Name) we have turned deep red; Maya's colour is a (fleeting) pale red;
(his) glance of grace has come, and the poison (of Maya) has been held back.
(My attention) has turned around (from Maya); dying while alive, I have awakened;
dwelling on him through the Shabad, the mind is attached to the Lord;
gathering the nectar (of the Name), I have cast the poison far off and given it up;
dwelling in (his) love, the fear of Jam has fled.
Cravings for taste, quarrelling and pride have ceased;
by the Hukam of the Infinite, the mind is dyed in the Lord;
the rites of caste and of (worldly) honour are left behind;
(his) gracious gaze has fallen, and the peace of the soul has taken hold.
Without you, (O Lord,) I see no friend.
Whom shall I serve? To whom shall I give my heart?
Whom shall I ask? At whose feet shall I fall?
By whose teaching shall I stay lovingly attuned?
I serve the Guru; at the Guru's feet I fall;
I practise devotion and am absorbed in the Lord's Name;
love is (my) teaching, (my) initiation and (my) food;
by (his) Hukam, through the union he ordains, I reach my own true home.
Pride is gone; there is peace in the soul's meditation (on him);
the light has dawned, and (my) light has merged in (his) Light;
what is written (on the heart) is not erased: the Shabad is its mark;
I have known both the Creator and the creation to be the Creator himself.
I am no pandit, nor clever, nor wise;
I do not stray, nor am I led astray by doubt;
I do not speak idle talk; I have recognised (his) Hukam;
through the Guru's teaching Nanak is merged in Sahaj.
221.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The mind is an elephant, roaming in the forest of the body;
the Guru is its goad; when the true Shabad is the mark (upon it),
it is adorned at the King's gate and is held in honour.
(The Lord) is not recognised through cleverness;
unless (the mind) is slain, how is (his) worth to be found?
Within the house (of the heart) is nectar, but the thief carries it off;
no one says no (to him);
the one whom (the Lord) himself protects, he blesses with honour.
Fires (of craving) beyond all counting are gathered in one place;
they were quenched with water (of the Name) when the Guru gave understanding;
I have gained it by giving my mind, and joyfully I sing (his) virtues.
As (the Lord) is at home, so is he outside;
then, sitting in a cave, how could I say he is any different?
The Fearless One is just the same in ocean and on mountain.
Say, who can slay the one who has died (to self)?
What fear, and of whom, can the fearless have?
Through the Shabad he recognises (the Lord in) the three worlds.
One who has only spoken has merely told a tale;
one who has understood has recognised (him) in Sahaj;
seeing and reflecting, my mind is won over.
Glory, beauty and liberation lie in praising the One;
there itself the Niranjan abides;
he pervades his own home, his own place.
Many a sage praises (him) with love,
with pure body and mind, holding the True One in the heart.
O Nanak, worship the Lord, day after day, for ever.
222.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The mind does not die (to itself), nor is the work (of life) fulfilled,
(for) the mind is in the grip of the demons (the vices), of evil intellect and of duality.
When the mind is won over through the Guru, it becomes one (with God).
The Lord, who is beyond the three qualities, comes under the sway of virtues;
one who casts off self reflects on him.
The mind gone astray thinks of vice upon vice;
the mind gone astray takes a load (of sin) upon its head.
When the mind is won over, it becomes one with the Lord, the One Creator, Ekankar.
The mind gone astray goes into the house of Maya;
entangled in lust, it does not stay in its place.
O mortal, worship the Lord, with your tongue steeped in (the Name's) savour.
Fine elephants and fine horses, gold, sons and wife:
in much anxiety (over them) one loses the bout in the arena (of life) and departs.
It is a gambler's game, in which the pieces stay unripe.
Hoarding wealth, vices arise;
joy and sorrow stand (ever) at the door.
Peace comes in Sahaj by repeating (the Name of) Murari in the heart.
When (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, he brings (one) into union (with himself);
(then,) gathering virtues, one burns away faults through the Shabad,
and through the Guru obtains the treasure of the Naam.
Without the Name, every pain comes to dwell (in one);
the foolish manmukh's mind dwells in Maya.
Wisdom through the Guru (comes to one) for whom it is written from the start, by (the Lord's) grace.
The fickle mind runs, and runs again;
the True and Pure One is not pleased by (this) filth.
O Nanak, through the Guru one sings the praises of the Lord.
222.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Living in Haumai, one finds no peace;
the mind's own counsel is false; he (the Lord) is true.
All who are fond of duality come to ruin;
(yet) one does what is written (for him) from the start.
Such a gambler is the world, as I have seen it:
forgetting the Name, it begs for every comfort.
Only if the Unseen is seen can (he) be described;
to speak (of him) without seeing goes for nothing.
Through the Guru he is seen, in Sahaj and in love,
when the mind is set on service and attuned in love to the One.
Begging for comfort, one only gets more pain,
(for) one strings a garland of every vice.
Without the One, the false find no release;
the Creator makes and makes (all), and himself watches over it.
One who puts out the fire of craving through the Shabad,
and, in Sahaj and in love, (puts out) the doubt of duality too,
enshrines the Naam in his heart through the Guru's teaching,
and through the true Bani sings the praises of the Lord.
The True One is within the body; love (for him) comes through the Guru.
Without the Name, (the mind) has no home of its own.
The Beloved Sovereign is ruled by love;
when he casts his glance of grace, then one understands the Name.
Attachment to Maya is nothing but entanglement;
the manmukh is filthy, despised and fearsome.
When one serves the True Guru, the entanglement ends,
and the nectar of the Naam, peace for ever, stays with one.
Through the Guru one understands, and attunes oneself in love to the One;
one dwells in one's own home (within) and merges in the True One;
one brings (the round of) birth and death to a halt;
one gains this wisdom from the Perfect Guru.
I speak (of him), but no end (of him) is reached;
I have asked the Guru and seen: there is no other door.
Pain and pleasure come by his will, by his command:
so says lowly Nanak, attuned (to him) in love.
223.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Maya, which breeds duality, dwells in the minds of the world;
lust, anger and pride (born of it) bring ruin.
Whom shall I call a second? There is none;
in all is that One, the Immaculate.
The evil intellect of duality speaks of two;
(one in its grip) comes and goes, and dying, stays apart (from God).
In earth and sky I see no second,
nor in woman or man, nor in all the world.
I behold the light of the lamps (of the world), the sun and the moon:
within all, through and through, is the ever-young Beloved.
In his grace (the True Guru) has fixed my mind (on God);
the True Guru has made me understand the One.
Through the Guru the One, the Immaculate, is known;
when duality is killed, he is recognised through the Shabad.
The Hukam of the One alone prevails in all the world;
from the One has all creation come.
The paths are two, (but) know that the Master (of both) is One;
through the Guru's Shabad, recognise (his) Hukam.
(He who is) in all forms and colours, and in (every) mind:
says Nanak, I praise that One alone.
223.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If one does the deeds of the spirit, then he is a true (yogi);
what can the unripe one know of the secret of liberation?
That yogi reflects on the (true) way
who kills the five (vices) and holds the True One in his heart.
One within whom (the Lord) makes the Truth dwell
knows the worth of the way of Yoga.
To him sun and moon, home and wilderness, are alike;
his practice is the praise (of God), as natural to him as his everyday deeds.
He begs for one alms alone, the one Shabad;
(in him) wisdom, meditation, the (true) way and the Truth awaken.
He stays steeped in the fear (of God) and does not stray outside (it);
who can tell the worth of one who stays attuned in love?
(The Lord) himself unites (him) and ends (his) doubt;
by the Guru's grace he attains the supreme state.
(He) serves the Guru and reflects on the Shabad,
and kills Haumai: this is the finest practice.
Repetition (jap), austerity, self-restraint, the reading of the Puranas:
says Nanak, (all these lie in) accepting the Infinite One.
223.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(Such yogis) have taken up forgiveness; good conduct and contentment are their vow;
no disease afflicts them, nor any torment from Jam;
they are set free, (one with) God, who is without form or outline.
What fear can there be for the yogi
(for whom) he alone is in the trees and plants, in the home and outside?
Fearless is the yogi who meditates on the Immaculate (Lord);
night and day he stays awake, and keeps his mind attuned to the True One;
that yogi is dear to my mind.
In the fire of Brahm (God) he burns up the net of death;
(the fear of) old age and death is gone, and he casts off pride;
he crosses over himself, and carries his ancestors across as well.
One who serves the True Guru is the yogi;
one who stays steeped in the fear (of God) becomes fearless;
as is the one he serves, so he becomes.
The Name of the Fearless One makes a person pure;
he makes masters of the masterless; I am a sacrifice (to him).
(For me) there is no birth again and again: I sing (his) praises.
He knows the One within and without;
through the Guru's Shabad he recognises his own self;
through the true Shabad he bears the mark (of acceptance) at (the Lord's) door.
One who dies through the Shabad comes to dwell in his own home (within);
he neither comes nor goes, and his hopes come to an end;
through the Guru's Shabad, the lotus (of his heart) blossoms.
Whoever is seen (in the world) is let down in his hopes,
(gripped by) the poison of lust and anger, by hunger and thirst.
O Nanak, rare are those found who stand detached.
224.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If one meets such a servant (of the Lord), peace comes;
pain is forgotten, and that one finds the True One.
Beholding (his) sight, the understanding is made whole;
the dust of (his) feet is (as) the bath at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.
(His) eyes are satisfied, the thread of (his) attention held on the One;
(his) tongue, (tasting) the Lord's sublime savour, is made pure.
Truth is (his) conduct, and within (his) heart is (the Lord's) service;
(his) mind is fulfilled in the Lord, unseen and unfathomable.
Wherever I look, there is the True One;
without understanding, the unripe world quarrels.
When the Guru explains, understanding dawns;
only some rare one understands (this) through the Guru.
In your mercy, O Protector, save (us);
without understanding, (people) have become beasts, out of step (with life's true rhythm).
The Guru has said there is no other, no second;
tell me, seeing whom should I worship another?
God has upheld the three worlds for the Sants' sake;
one who recognises his own self reflects on this essence.
One in whose heart is the True One, in whom true love dwells:
Nanak humbly prays: I am his servant.
224.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Brahma grew proud, and did not know (the Lord);
when the calamity of (losing) the Vedas fell upon him, he repented;
when he remembered God, only then was his mind convinced.
Pride is such an evil in the world;
whoever meets the Guru, (the Guru) removes his pride.
King Bali, proud of his wealth (Maya),
performed sacrifices, swollen with a heavy load of pride;
without asking his guru, he went down to the netherworld.
Harichand gave alms and won renown;
(yet) without the Guru he did not find the end of the inscrutable (Lord).
(God) himself leads astray, and himself gives understanding.
Harnakhash, of evil mind, was a doer of evil deeds;
God, Narayan, is the destroyer of pride:
he showed mercy and saved Prahlad.
Ravan, a fool, went astray in his heedlessness;
Lanka was plundered, and his heads went with it;
he perished in pride, without love for the True Guru.
Sahasbahu, Madhu and Kaitabh, Mahikhasur,
and Harnakhash, whom (the Lord) seized and tore apart with his nails:
these demons were slain, without the practice of devotion.
Jarasandh and Kalyavan were slain;
Raktabij and Kalnem were torn apart;
slaying the demons, (the Lord) carried the Sants across.
He himself, as the True Guru, reflects on the Shabad;
in the love of another, the demons were slain;
and the Gurmukhs, through true devotion, he carried across.
Duryodhan drowned, and lost his honour;
he did not know the Lord, who alone is the Creator;
for the pain he gives the Lord's servant, a man is consumed, and the pain is his own.
Janmejay did not understand the Guru's word;
lost in doubt, how could he find peace?
He erred by no more than a sesame seed, and then repented.
Kans, Keshi and Chandur, none was (their equal in might);
(but) they did not recognise the Lord, and lost their honour;
without the Master of the world, no one can save (anyone).
Without the Guru, pride cannot be erased;
through the Guru's teaching, (attuned) to the Lord's Name, one gains righteousness and patience;
O Nanak, singing (God's) praises, one receives the Name.
225.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(If) I rub perfume and sandalwood upon my body,
(and) put on silk and silken robes and wear them out,
(still) without the Lord's Name, where could I find peace?
Why should I wear (fine clothes)? Why put them on and show them off?
Without the Master of the world, where can I find peace?
(If I had) rings in my ears and a string of pearls at my neck,
a red quilt and red flowers (strewn upon it),
without the Master of the world, where would I seek peace?
(If there were) a beautiful woman with lovely eyes,
decked with the sixteen adornments and very dear (to me),
without remembering the Master of the world, there is ever ruin.
Gates, houses, palaces, a comfortable bed,
on which a gardener strews flowers day and night:
without the Lord's Name, that body is a home of suffering.
Fine horses, fine elephants, lances, martial music,
armies, deputies, royal servants, all this show:
without the Master of the world, (such) displays are false.
(If) I am called a Siddha, and summon the riddhis and siddhis,
(if) I set a crown and a royal cap upon my head and a canopy over it,
without the Master of the world, where would I find the Truth?
(If) I am called a khan, an emperor, a king,
(and) order (my servants) about, it is a false show;
without the Guru's Shabad, (life's) purpose will not be fulfilled.
Haumai and the sense of mine are forgotten through the Guru's Shabad;
through the Guru's teaching I have known Murari in my heart.
Nanak humbly prays: (I have come) to your refuge.
225.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(He serves) the One alone, and knows no other;
he gives up the bitter ills of the world's show;
through love he meets the True One, and in the True One he becomes true, O brother.
Such is the Lord's devotee, his servant:
singing the Lord's praises, he meets (him), and washes away (his) filth.
The (heart-)lotus of the whole world is upside down;
the fire of evil counsel burns the world through and through;
he alone is saved who reflects on the Shabad of the Guru.
The bumble-bee, the moth, the elephant and the fish,
and the deer die, each bearing (the fruit of) what it has done;
absorbed in craving, they did not see what is real.
The lover of women thinks only of lust,
and anger destroys all who are given to vice;
forgetting the Name, they lose their honour and their understanding.
The manmukh lets his mind waver toward another's home;
the noose is about his neck, and he is caught up in worldly affairs;
through the Guru, singing the Lord's praises, he will be set free.
As a widow gives her body to a stranger,
and, for lust or for money, puts her mind in another's power,
(yet) without her husband she is never satisfied; (so it is with the soul without the Lord).
One reads and reads books, the Simritis, the recitations,
reads the Vedas and the Puranas and hears their compositions,
(yet) without being dyed in the (Lord's) sweet essence, the mind plays out many a show.
As the chatrik thirsts in love for the water,
as the fish delights in the water,
O Nanak, (the Lord's devotee) is satisfied, drinking the Lord's sweet essence.
226.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who wears himself out with hath (forced austerities) is not counted (in the Lord's account);
he puts on many a garb and smears (his body with) ashes;
forgetting the Name, he repents in the end.
Keep the dear Lord in your mind, and you will have peace in your mind;
forgetting the Name, you will suffer the pains (inflicted by) Jam.
(One absorbed in) perfume, sandalwood, aloeswood and camphor
is intoxicated with Maya, and the supreme state is far (from him);
when the Name is forgotten, all is falsehood, utterly false.
Lances, martial music, the throne, salutes:
(with these) craving only grows, and lust takes hold;
without begging (them) of the Lord, there is neither devotion nor the Name.
In wrangling and in pride there is no meeting with God;
giving your mind, you will receive the Name, the source of ease;
in the love of another there is ignorance, the source of pain.
Without money there is no buying in the shop;
without a ship there is no way across the ocean;
without serving the Guru there is loss upon loss.
Praise, praise to the one (the Guru) who shows the way;
praise, praise to the one who makes the Shabad heard;
praise, praise to the one who unites (us) in union (with the Lord).
Praise, praise to the One to whom this soul belongs;
through the Guru's Shabad, churn (it) and drink the Amrit;
in his will, he will give you the glory of the Name.
Without the Name, how can I live, O mother?
May I keep repeating (your Name) night and day, (staying) in your refuge.
O Nanak, steeped in the Name, one gains honour.
226.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Acting in Haumai, the wearers of religious garb have not known (the Lord);
through the Guru, rare is the one whose mind is won over to devotion.
Crying I, I, the True One is not found;
when Haumai goes, the supreme state is attained.
In Haumai, kings march out time and again (against one another);
in Haumai they are ruined; they are born, die and come again.
Haumai is driven out (of one who) reflects on the Guru's Shabad;
he gives up the fickle intellect, and slays the five (passions).
Those with the True One within come home to Sahaj;
knowing the Sovereign (Lord), they attain the supreme state.
Truth becomes his way of life, and the Guru removes his doubt;
he sits in deep absorption in the home of the Fearless One.
Dying while crying I, I, what does one gain?
One who meets the Perfect Guru puts an end to that strife.
Whatever there is, all of it is nothing;
the Gurmukhs, receiving (divine) wisdom, sing (the Lord's) praises.
Haumai binds (beings) in bonds and makes them wander (in births);
O Nanak, through devotion to the Lord one finds peace.
227.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
First of all, Brahma himself came into the house of death;
(going down) to the netherworld, he did not find (the end of) the lotus of his birth;
he did not heed the command; lost in doubt, he went astray.
Whoever is born is slain by death;
the Lord has kept me safe, for I have reflected on the Guru's Shabad.
Maya has enticed all the goddesses and gods;
death does not let (anyone) go without service of the Guru;
he (the Lord) alone is imperishable, beyond sight, beyond knowing.
Sultans, khans and kings are not to remain;
one who strays from the Name must bear the pain (inflicted by) Jam;
my support is the Name; as you keep me, so I remain.
Chaudharis and kings: none has a lasting abode (here);
bankers die, heaping up Maya and money;
give me, O Lord, the wealth of the Amrit Name.
Subjects, headmen, village heads and chiefs:
none is seen to stay unmoved in the world;
unstoppable death strikes the false upon the head.
The One alone is unmoving, the truest True One;
he who made and fashioned (the world), he alone destroys it all;
when he becomes known through the Guru, then there is honour.
Qazis, sheikhs, fakirs in religious garb
call themselves great, (but) the pain of Haumai is in their bodies;
death does not let (them) go without the support of the True Guru.
The net of death lies in the tongue and in the eyes;
death is in the ears, (when one) hears words of poison;
without the Shabad, (all) are robbed day and night.
When the True One dwells in the heart through the Lord's Name,
death cannot even eye (one who) sings (his) praises;
O Nanak, through the Guru one merges in the Shabad.
227.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those who speak the truth, with not a mustard seed of falsehood in them,
who, through the Guru, walk in the Hukam of the Master of the Will,
remain detached (from Maya), in the refuge of the True One.
One who settles in the home of Truth is not eyed by death;
but the manmukh, through attachment, suffers the pain of coming and going.
Drinking the Amrit and speaking (the praise) of the Ineffable, one stays (in the true home);
sitting in one's own home within, one finds the home of Sahaj;
steeped in the Lord's essence, one can say: this is (true) peace.
The way of living by the Guru's teaching is steadfast; it does not waver;
by the Guru's teaching one utters (the Name of) the Lord, (rooted) in the True One, in Sahaj;
he drinks the Amrit and churns out the essence.
(I) beheld the True Guru and took (his) teaching;
I offered (him) mind and body, and took (that teaching) deep within;
I came to know (his) state and extent, (and) recognised my own self.
The Name of the Stainless One is the finest food;
(living on it, one) becomes a true Param Hans, (lit by) the Light of the Infinite;
wherever I look, there is the One Creator, Ekankar.
(Such a one) stays detached, leaning on no (worldly) support; (remembering) the One True Lord is his only practice;
serving at the Guru's feet, he has attained the supreme state;
his mind is won over from within itself, and the wandering of ego has ended.
Who is there whom this way has not carried across?
The Lord's praise has carried the Sants and devotees across.
I have found God; I have sought no other.
In the true mansion the Guru has made the Unseen seen (by me);
that mansion is unshakeable; no shadow of Maya falls (there);
content in the True One, (I) have been rid of doubt.
Those in whose minds that True One has come to dwell —
their company is found through the Guru;
O Nanak, in the True Name (their) filth is washed away.
228.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One whose mind is dyed in the Lord, in the Name —
on rising at dawn, one should have the sight of him.
If you do not repeat (the Name of) Ram, it is your misfortune;
age after age our God, Ram, is the Giver.
The one who repeats (the Name of) Ram by the Guru's teaching is perfect;
in that heart the unstruck music plays.
Those who are (absorbed) in devotion to Ram, in love of the Lord —
God, in his grace, has protected them.
Those in whose hearts that Lord, Har Har, (dwells) —
by having the sight of them, peace is found.
The One pervades all beings;
(yet) the proud manmukh wanders through births again and again.
He alone understands (this) who finds the True Guru;
he kills his Haumai, and through the Guru's Shabad finds (God).
How can (one) know the union of the lower (soul) with the higher (God)?
Through the Guru this union is found, and the mind is won over.
(O God,) bless us sinners, devoid of virtue, with virtue;
when God becomes merciful, servant Nanak crosses over.
The sixteen Ashtapadis of Gauri Guareri.
228.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
As a herdsman (guards) his cows, so you guard (your creatures) with care;
day and night you nourish and protect (them), and grant the peace of the soul.
Keep (me) safe here and hereafter, O Merciful to the meek;
(I have come) to your refuge; look on (me) with your glance of grace.
Wherever I look, you are pervading; keep (me), O Keeper.
You are the Giver, you yourself the Enjoyer; you are the prop of the breath of life.
Without reflection on divine wisdom, (one is tossed) down and up by the record of past deeds;
without praising the Lord of the world, the darkness does not end.
I have watched the world perish in greed and pride;
by serving the Guru, God is found, and the true door of liberation.
The mansion of the Infinite is in one's own home within; he is beyond the beyond.
Without the Shabad no one stays steady; one who understands (this) finds peace.
What did you bring, and what will you take away? (Yet) you are caught in the net of Jam;
like a bucket bound fast to a rope, (you go up) to the sky and (down) to the underworld.
If, by the Guru's teaching, the Naam is not forgotten, honour comes in Sahaj;
within is the treasure, the Shabad; meeting (him), one sheds self-conceit.
When God casts his glance of grace, (one) merges in the embrace of the Virtuous One.
O Nanak, (that) union is never broken; (such a one) earns the true profit.
229.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If, by the Guru's grace, you come to understand (this), then (your account) is settled:
in every heart (dwells) the Name of the Stainless One; he is my Master.
Without the Guru's Shabad there is no release; reflect and see.
Though (you) perform a hundred thousand rites, without the Guru there is darkness.
The blind, bereft of understanding — what can be said to them?
Without the Guru the path is not seen; how is (the journey) to be carried through?
(Such a one) calls the false coin true, and knows nothing of what the true is worth;
the blind man is named an assayer — such is the strange way of Kalyug.
(The world) calls the sleeper awake, and the wakeful asleep;
it calls the living dead, and does not weep for the dead.
The one coming (to God's path) it calls gone, and the one gone (from it) it calls arrived;
it calls what is another's its own, and what is its own does not please it.
It calls the sweet bitter, and the bitter sweet;
(people) slander the one dyed (in the Lord's love) — this is how I have seen Kalyug.
(People) serve the handmaid (Maya), and the Master is not seen (by them);
if the water of a pond is churned, no butter comes of it.
Whoever grasps the meaning of this verse, he is my Guru.
O Nanak, one who recognises his own self is (one with) the Lord, beyond all and without limit.
(God) himself is at work in all; he himself has led (beings) astray in doubt.
By the Guru's grace it is understood that God is contained in all.
229.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The mind's Sutak is the love of another (than God);
strayed in (this) doubt, (people) keep coming and going.
The manmukh's Sutak never departs,
as long as he is not drenched, through the Shabad, in the Lord's Name.
All is Sutak, as much as there is of attachment and the visible world;
(caught in it, one) dies and is born, over and over.
Sutak is in fire, in air and in water;
Sutak is all the food that (people) eat.
Under Sutak, no rite or worship can be done;
imbued with the Naam, the mind becomes pure.
By serving the True Guru, Sutak departs;
(then one) neither dies nor is born, and death does not devour (him).
Let anyone search the Shastras and Simritis and see:
without the Name, no one is set free.
In all four ages the Naam is supreme, (found) by reflecting on the Shabad;
in Kalyug the Gurmukh reaches the far shore.
The True One does not die, nor come and go;
O Nanak, the Gurmukh remains merged (in him).
229.3: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through the Guru, (the Lord's) service is the prop of the breath of life;
keep the dear Lord in your heart, held to your breast;
through the Guru there is glory at the True One's door.
O Pandit, read (the Name of) the Lord, and give up your vices;
through the Guru, cross the terrifying world-ocean.
Through the Guru, Haumai departs from within;
through the Guru, no filth comes to cling (to the mind);
through the Guru, the Naam comes to dwell in the mind.
Through the Guru, (one's) deeds and dharam come to rest in the True One;
through the Guru, (one) burns away pride and duality;
through the Guru, imbued with the Naam, one is at peace.
Awaken your own mind, and understand him;
you instruct the people, (but) no one listens;
understand through the Guru, and there will be lasting peace.
The manmukh is full of show and cleverness;
whatever he does is not accepted;
he comes and goes, and finds no resting place.
The manmukh performs rites, in great pride;
like a crane he sits every day in meditation;
when Jam seized him, only then did he repent.
Without serving the True Guru there is no liberation;
by the Guru's grace that Lord is met;
in all four ages the Guru is the Giver (of the Name).
For the Gurmukh, caste, honour and greatness lie in the Naam alone;
(he) has torn apart and cast away the daughter of the ocean (Maya).
O Nanak, without the Name all cleverness is false.
230.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O brothers, study the dharam of this age:
the perfect Guru has given full understanding:
here and hereafter the Lord's Name is the companion.
Read (the Name of) Ram, and reflect (on him) in your mind;
by the Guru's grace, remove (the mind's) filth.
By argument and opposition (God) is not found;
in the love of another, mind and body grow insipid;
through the Guru's Shabad, fix your loving attention on the True One.
This world is soiled with Haumai;
it bathes daily at places of pilgrimage, (yet) its pride does not go;
without meeting the Guru, Jam brings it to ruin.
True is that person who kills his Haumai;
who, through the Guru's Shabad, destroys the five (passions);
he himself swims across and carries all his families across.
Through attachment to Maya, the Juggler (God) has staged (the world's) show;
the blind manmukhs stay clinging (to it);
the Gurmukhs, their attention fixed (on God), remain untouched.
The wearer of religious garb puts on many guises;
(but) within him is craving, and he goes about in pride;
he does not know himself, and loses the game (of life).
Wearing (holy) garments, he plays clever;
through attachment to Maya he is gravely misled by doubt;
without serving the Guru he suffers great pain.
Those imbued with the Naam are ever detached;
even within the household, their loving attention stays fixed on the True One.
O Nanak, great is the fortune of those who serve the True Guru.
230.2: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Brahma is the root of the study of the Vedas;
from him the gods were born, (caught) in attachment and craving;
they wandered in the three qualities, and did not come to dwell in their own home (within).
The Lord has saved us, and brought us to meet the True Guru,
(who) has made devotion, night and day, and the Lord's Name firm (within us).
The word of Brahma (the Vedas) is of the three qualities, an entanglement (of Maya);
reading it, (the pandits) hold forth in dispute, and Jamkaal strikes them on the head;
they do not recognise the essence, and tie up bundles of straw.
The manmukhs, through ignorance, are set on the wrong path;
they have forgotten the Lord's Name, and hold fast to many rites;
in the love of another, they have drowned in the world-ocean.
One who is beholden to Maya calls himself a pandit;
steeped in the poison (of Maya), he suffers great pain;
around his neck is the noose of Jam, and death torments him always.
Jamkaal does not come near the Gurmukh;
through the Shabad he burns away Haumai and duality;
dyed in the Naam alone, he sings the Lord's praises.
Maya, (as) a maidservant, does the work of the devotees;
whoever falls at (their) feet attains (the Lord's) mansion;
he is ever pure, and remains merged in Sahaj.
Those who listen to the telling of the Lord's praises are seen to be the wealthy in the world;
all bow before them, and revere them night and day;
(for) in Sahaj they dwell on the True One's virtues in their minds.
The perfect True Guru made (one) hear the Shabad,
erased (his) three qualities, and fixed (his) mind on the fourth (state);
O Nanak, killing (his) Haumai, (the Guru) united (him) with Brahm (God).
231.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(The pandit) reads Brahma's Veda, and holds forth in dispute;
within him is the darkness of tamas, and he does not know himself;
he finds God only when he utters the Guru's Shabad.
I serve the Guru, and then death does not devour (me);
the manmukhs, in the love of another, are devoured (by it).
Through the Guru, (even) sinful mortals have succeeded;
through the Guru's Shabad they are delighted within, in Sahaj;
they have found my God; through the Guru's Shabad they have succeeded.
Those whom the True Guru has joined, God himself has united (with him);
they are dear to the mind of my True God;
in Sahaj and in love, they sing the Lord's praises.
Without the True Guru, (people) are led astray by doubt;
the blind manmukhs eat poison always;
they bear the rod of Jam, and suffer pain always.
Poor Jam cannot even look at one who is in the Lord's refuge;
killing his Haumai, he keeps his loving attention on the True One;
he stays ever attuned to the Lord's Name.
Those who serve the True Guru are spotless and holy;
joining (their) mind to (the Guru's) mind, they have conquered the whole world;
in this way, my friend, there will be well-being in you (too).
Whoever serves the True Guru obtains (this) fruit:
the Naam (dwells) in his heart, and he sheds self-conceit from within;
he makes the Shabad, the unstruck Bani, resound (within).
Who, who has not succeeded through the True Guru, my brother?
through devotion they have succeeded, and won glory at (the Lord's) door;
O Nanak, greatness lies in the Name of Ram.
231.2: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who expounds only the three qualities: his doubt does not go;
his bonds do not break, and he does not obtain liberation;
the giver of liberation in the world is the True Guru.
Through the Guru, the mortal sheds his doubt;
with loving attention fixed on the Lord, the strain of Sahaj wells up (within).
Over the heads of (those caught in) the three qualities, death holds sway;
they do not remember the Name of the Creator;
they die and are born, again and again, time after time.
From a blind guru doubt does not go;
leaving the Root (God), (his followers) cling to the love of another;
drunk on poison, (one) is absorbed in poison.
Taking Maya to be the root (of life), creatures wander astray;
in the love of another they have forgotten the dear Lord;
the one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace attains the supreme state.
Within him is the Truth, and outwardly too he deals in Truth;
Truth does not stay hidden, though one may keep it hidden;
the wise understand (this), in Sahaj and in love.
The Gurmukh keeps his loving attention fixed on the True One;
through the Shabad he burns away Haumai and Maya;
my True God unites him in (his) union.
(One whom) the True Guru, the Giver, makes hear the Shabad
keeps the running (mind) safe, and holds it back and still;
from the perfect Guru he obtains understanding.
He himself is the Creator, who created the world and (himself) destroyed it;
apart from him there is no other at all;
O Nanak, through the Guru, a rare one understands (this).
232.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Gurmukh obtains the priceless Naam;
he serves the Naam alone, and through the Naam remains merged in Sahaj;
with his tongue he ever sings the Amrit Naam;
the one on whom (God) shows grace obtains the Lord's sweet essence.
Night and day I repeat (the Name of) the Lord of the world in my heart;
through the Guru I attain the supreme state of peace.
In (their) hearts there is peace, and light has dawned,
who through the Guru sing of the True One, the treasure of virtues;
they ever become the servants of the servants' servants;
in household and family they remain ever detached.
A rare Gurmukh becomes liberated while yet alive;
he alone obtains the supreme treasure;
erasing the three qualities, he becomes pure;
in Sahaj, (absorbed) in the True One, he meets that very God.
Attachment and love for family no longer hold (him)
when that True One comes to dwell in the heart;
through the Guru, the mind pierced (with love) becomes steady;
he recognises (God's) Hukam, and understands that True One.
(O God,) you are the Creator; for me there is no other;
I serve you, and from you comes honour;
if you show grace, I may sing of that God;
the jewel of the Naam is the light in all the world.
(One to whom) through the Guru the Bani has come to taste sweet:
his heart within blossoms, and his loving attention stays fixed night and day;
by (God's) grace he meets the True One in Sahaj;
it is by perfect great fortune that the True Guru is found.
Haumai, possessiveness, evil-mindedness and pain are destroyed
when the Name of Ram, the treasure of virtues, (dwells) in the heart.
Through the Guru, with God's praise, the intellect awakens,
when (God) pervades the heart, and (one) dwells at (his) feet.
He alone obtains the Naam to whom (God) gives it;
the one whom (God) unites (with him) through the Guru sheds his self-conceit;
he enshrines the True Name in his heart;
O Nanak, in Sahaj he merges in the True One.
232.2: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(One who) has set the mind right within itself, in (God's) fear, in Sahaj and in love,
(who) has dyed the mind with the Shabad, fixing his loving attention,
dwells in his own home (within), in God's will.
Serving the True Guru, pride departs,
and Govind, the treasure of virtues, is found.
The mind becomes detached when, through the Shabad, it takes in (God's) fear;
my pure God is pervading everywhere;
by the Guru's grace, one whom (he) unites meets (him).
The servant of the Lord's servants finds peace;
in this way my Lord God is found;
by the Lord's grace (he) sings the praises of Ram.
Cursed is a long life in which love for the Lord's Name does not take hold;
cursed is the comfortable bed with a wife, (if it is) only the pitch darkness of attachment;
fruitful is the birth of those whose support is the Naam.
Cursed, cursed are the home and family in which there is no love for the Lord;
he alone is my friend who sings the praises of that Lord;
without the Lord's Name I have no other.
I have obtained liberation and honour from the True Guru;
I have meditated on the Lord's Name, and erased all pain;
with loving attention fixed on the Lord's Name, there is lasting bliss.
Meeting the Guru, I have come to awareness of the body;
the whole fire of Haumai and craving has been put out;
anger is destroyed, and (I) have taken hold of forgiveness.
The Lord himself shows grace and gives the Naam;
a rare Gurmukh receives (this) jewel;
Nanak sings the praises of the Lord, unseen and unfathomable.
233.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who turn their faces from the True Guru, those faithless ones, look evil;
bound (by attachment), they are beaten night and day, and do not get the chance again.
O Lord, O Lord, show your grace and keep (me) safe;
O God, O Lord, unite (me) with the Sat Sangat, that (I may) cherish the Lord's virtues in my heart.
Those devotees are dear to the Lord who, through the Guru, walk in love;
giving up self-conceit, they serve, and remain dead while living.
He to whom body and breath belong: his service is laid on (our) heads;
why should we forget him from the mind? Let us keep the Lord enshrined in the heart.
When the Naam is found, honour is gained; when the Naam is taken to heart, there is peace;
the Naam is obtained from the True Guru, and that God is met by (his) grace.
Those who turn their faces from the True Guru wander, and never find rest;
neither earth nor sky will bear them; they lie in filth and rot.
This world, given the thugs' drug of attachment, is led astray by doubt;
those who have met the True Guru: Maya does not come near to touch them.
Those who serve the True Guru are beautiful, having shed the filth of Haumai;
those dyed in the Shabad are pure, and walk in the True Guru's will.
O Lord God, you alone are the Giver; you yourself forgive and unite (us with you);
your servant Nanak has come to your refuge; as it pleases you, so set (him) free.
234.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, Karhale, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O camel-mind, O wanderer in foreign lands, how may one meet the Lord, the Mother?
(One who) found the Guru through perfect fortune, the Beloved came and embraced (him).
O camel-mind, meditate on the True Guru, the great Being.
O thoughtful camel-mind, meditate on the Name of the Lord, Ram;
where the account (of deeds) is called for, the Lord himself will set (you) free.
O camel-mind, (you were) utterly pure; the filth of Haumai has come and stuck (to you).
The beloved Husband is plainly present with (you), in (your own) home; (yet the soul,) parted (from him), suffers blows.
O camel-mind, my beloved, search for the Lord in (your) heart, and search until you find (him).
He is not found by any (other) means; it is the Guru who shows the Lord in the heart.
O camel-mind, my beloved, keep your attention fixed lovingly on the Lord, day and night.
(Then) you will go and find your home in the palace of delight; the Guru unites (you), brings (you) into union with the Lord.
O camel-mind, you are my friend: give up hypocrisy and greed.
The hypocrite and the greedy are beaten down; Jam's club deals out (their) punishment.
O camel-mind, my very life, cast off filth, hypocrisy and doubt.
The Guru has filled the pool of the Lord's Amrit (to the brim); joining the Sangat (and bathing there), the filth is washed off.
O camel-mind, my beloved, listen to one teaching of the Guru:
this attachment to Maya is spread (all around), (yet) at the end none of it goes along.
O camel-mind, my friend, (whoever) took the Lord's (Name) as provisions (for the journey) gained honour;
in the Lord's court he was robed (in honour), and the Lord himself took him in his embrace.
O camel-mind, with faith in the Guru, do the work (he bids), through the Guru.
Make your plea before the Guru, O servant Nanak: (O Guru,) unite me with the Lord.
234.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O thoughtful camel-mind, reflect, and look with care:
the forest-dwellers have grown weary roaming the forests; (you,) through the Guru's teaching, behold the Husband (Lord) in your heart.
O camel-mind, cherish the Guru, Govind, (in your heart).
O thoughtful camel-mind, the manmukhs are caught in the great net (of Maya);
a Gurmukh soul is free, cherishing the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
O camel-mind, my beloved, seek out the True Guru in the Sat Sangat.
Clinging to the Sat Sangat, let us meditate on the Lord; the Lord, Har Har, will go along with you.
O fortunate camel-mind, the Lord looks (on one) with a single glance of grace;
only if he himself sets (one) free is (one) freed; cherish the True Guru's feet.
O camel-mind, my beloved, cherish the Light within the body.
The Guru has shown the Naam, the nine treasures; the merciful Lord has bestowed (this) gift.
O camel-mind, you are restless: give up your fearful cleverness.
Cherish the Name of the Lord, Har Har; when the end comes, the Lord (alone) will set (you) free.
O fortunate camel-mind, cherish the jewel of (divine) wisdom.
(Whoever) has taken the sword of the Guru's wisdom in hand has struck Jam dead with (that sword,) the death of Jam.
The treasure is within, O camel-mind, (yet) you wander in doubt, searching outside.
(One who) met the Guru, the perfect Being, found the Lord, the Friend, right with (him).
O camel-mind, steeped in (the world's) pleasures, cherish the Lord's love always.
The Lord's love never fades; serve the Guru and cherish the Shabad.
We are birds, O camel-mind; the Lord, the timeless Being, is the tree (we rest on).
The fortunate have found (him) through the Guru; O servant Nanak, cherish the Naam.
235.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace.
When this (person) is proud in his mind,
then he goes about crazed, a stranger (to all).
When he became the dust (of the feet) of all,
from then on he recognised the all-pervading Lord (Ramaiya) in every heart.
The fruit of humility is the ease of Sahaj;
my True Guru has given me (this humility) as a gift.
When he thinks someone is bad,
then everyone sets snares for him.
When he put an end to mine and yours,
from then on no one bears him enmity.
When he held fast to his own (interest) alone,
then he is in heavy trouble.
When he recognised the Creator,
then no burning envy at all is left in him.
When he made his attachment (to the world) fast,
he comes and goes (in birth and death), ever watched by Jam.
When all his doubts were destroyed,
he is no different from the Supreme Lord.
When he took distinctions to be something (real),
from then on (come) pain, punishment and torment.
When he understood the One alone,
from then on he came to understand everything.
When he runs about, a beggar for Maya,
he is never sated, and his thirst never leaves.
When he turned away from her,
Kaula (Lakshmi, Maya) rose and followed close behind him.
When, showing his grace, the True Guru met (him),
the lamp was lit in the temple of the mind;
understanding came of victory and defeat,
and then the worth of this house (the body) was known.
The One alone does and causes all to be done, everything;
he himself is the understanding, and he himself reflects and discerns.
He is not far; he is near, with all.
O Nanak, the Lord of all wonders is true and worthy of praise.
236.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through serving the Guru one is joined to the Naam;
(the Naam) comes to him on whose forehead (good) fortune is written.
In his heart he (the Lord) comes to dwell,
and (his) mind and body become cool and steady.
Sing such Kirtan, O my mind,
as will be of use to you here and there (hereafter).
Repeating his Name, fear and misfortune depart,
and the wandering mind comes to rest;
repeating his Name, pain never touches one again;
repeating his Name, this Haumai flees;
repeating his Name, the five (passions) come under control;
repeating his Name, Amrit is gathered in the heart;
repeating his Name, this craving is quenched;
repeating his Name, one succeeds in the Lord's court;
repeating his Name, millions of wrongs are wiped out;
repeating his Name, (people) become the Lord's Saadhs;
repeating his Name, the mind becomes cool;
repeating his Name, one rids oneself of all filth;
repeating his Name, the jewel, the Lord, is found,
and one grows so close to the Lord that one never leaves (him) again;
repeating his Name, (one gains) a dwelling (as) in many Baikunths (heavens);
repeating his Name, one dwells in peace and Sahaj;
repeating his Name, this fire (of craving) does not touch one;
repeating his Name, this death does not cast its eye on one;
repeating his Name, your forehead will be spotless;
repeating his Name, all pain is lifted;
repeating his Name, no difficulty arises;
repeating his Name, one hears the unstruck melody;
repeating his Name, one gains this spotless renown;
repeating his Name, the (inverted) lotus (of the heart) turns upright.
The Guru has cast his kindly glance upon all;
(but) he in whose heart (the Guru) places the mantra of the Lord
has made the unbroken Kirtan his food, his churi (sweet crumbled bread);
says Nanak, (this comes to him) whose True Guru is perfect.
236.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who) holds the Guru's Shabad within his heart,
breaks off company with the five (passions),
keeps the ten organs (of sense and action) under control,
in his soul the light shines.
Such firmness comes in him
on whom is the kindness and grace of that God.
To whom friend and foe are one and the same,
all his speaking is (divine) wisdom,
all his hearing is the Naam,
all his seeing is meditation (on God).
In Sahaj he wakes, in Sahaj he sleeps;
whatever comes to pass comes to pass (for him) in Sahaj;
in Sahaj is (his) sorrow, and in Sahaj too (his) laughter;
in Sahaj (his) silence, and in Sahaj too (his) chanting (of the Name).
In Sahaj (he takes his) food, in Sahaj (he gives his) love;
in Sahaj all (his) concealment has gone;
in Sahaj came the Saadh's company;
in Sahaj he met the Supreme Lord face to face.
In Sahaj he is at home, in Sahaj detached;
in Sahaj the duality in (his) body has been destroyed.
One in whose mind joy has arisen through Sahaj
has met (the Lord), the Supreme Bliss.
In Sahaj he has drunk the Amrit, the Naam;
in Sahaj he has given (others) the gift (of the Naam);
his soul has delighted in the discourse of Sahaj,
and the Imperishable has come to dwell with him.
In Sahaj the steady seat has pleased him;
in Sahaj he has sounded the unstruck Shabad;
in Sahaj the tinkling chime (of bliss) is lovely;
in his home (within) the Supreme Lord is pervading.
One on whom (the Lord's) grace has fallen in Sahaj
has met the Guru in Sahaj, and (gained) the true dharma.
Only one in whom Sahaj has arisen knows (it);
servant Nanak is a sacrifice to him.
237.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
First (the creature) is released from its dwelling in the womb;
(then) it is bound up with sons, wife and family;
(it enjoys) food of many kinds and many clothes;
(yet such) poor wretches will surely depart.
What is that place which never passes away?
What is that Shabad through which evil counsel is taken away?
In Indra's city (too) death is certain;
Brahma's city will not stay unmoved;
Shiv's city (too) will come to its end;
(the world) of Maya's three qualities, fallen out of tune, perishes.
Mountains, trees, earth, sky and stars;
sun, moon, wind, fire and water;
day and night, fasts and their many rules;
the Shastras, the Simritis and the Vedas: (all these) will perish.
Places of pilgrimage, gods, temples, holy books;
rosaries, frontal marks, the ritually pure kitchen, the priests of the fire offering;
the yogi's cleansing (dhoti), prostrations, the pleasures of palaces;
(all these and) the whole world will depart.
Castes, varnas, Muslims and Hindus;
beasts, birds, the creatures of countless species;
all the expanse that is seen spread out:
every visible form will perish.
(Where there is) praise sung in Sahaj, devotion, and knowledge of the Essence (God),
there is bliss for ever; that place is unmoving and true.
There the Saadh Sangat savours (the Lord's) virtues;
there the city without fear is ever inhabited.
There, neither fear nor doubt, sorrow nor worry;
no coming and going, and no death;
there is bliss for ever, and gatherings where the unstruck (music) sounds;
the devotees dwell there, upheld by Kirtan.
The Supreme Lord has no end and no far shore;
who can contemplate him?
Says Nanak, the one on whom (God) bestows grace
(finds) the unmoving place, and in the Saadh Sangat swims across (the world-ocean).
237.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Whoever kills this (duality), he alone is the hero;
Whoever kills this, he alone is complete;
Whoever kills this, to him comes honour;
Whoever kills this, his pain departs.
Rare is the one who kills duality and casts it out;
killing it, he practises Raj Jog.
Whoever kills this, he has no fear;
Those who kill this merge in the Naam;
Whoever kills this, his craving is quenched;
Whoever kills this, he succeeds in the Lord's court.
Whoever kills this, he is rich;
Whoever kills this, he is held in honour;
Whoever kills this, he alone is the (true) celibate;
Whoever kills this, he attains the high spiritual state.
Whoever kills this, his coming (into the world) is counted (as fruitful);
Whoever kills this, he stands steady, a man of (true) wealth;
Whoever kills this, he is greatly fortunate;
Whoever kills this, he stays awake night and day.
Whoever kills this, he is liberated while yet alive;
Whoever kills this, his way of life is pure;
Whoever kills this, he alone is truly wise;
Whoever kills this, he keeps his meditation fixed in Sahaj.
Without killing this, (one) is not accepted,
though he performs millions of rites, chants and austerities;
without killing this, (the round of) birth does not end;
without killing this, (one) is not freed from Jam.
Without killing this, there is no divine knowledge;
without killing this, (the mind's) impurity is not washed away;
without killing this, everything is soiled;
without killing this, everything stays apart (from God).
The one to whom (God), the treasure of mercy, has been merciful
is set free, and has gained success in all.
The one whose duality the Guru has killed,
says Nanak, contemplates God.
238.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If one is joined to the Lord, everyone is a friend;
If one is joined to the Lord, the mind becomes steady;
If one is joined to the Lord, no worry takes hold;
If one is joined to the Lord, there is deliverance.
O my mind, join yourself to the Lord;
nothing else will serve you at all.
The great men of the world,
those fools, are of no use at all;
the Lord's servant may be heard of as one of low birth,
(yet) in his company (people) are saved in an instant.
Hearing whose Name is (worth) millions of (holy) baths,
meditating on whom is (worth) millions of acts of worship,
hearing the Lord's Bani brings millions of merits;
knowing from the Guru the way (to meet him) yields millions of fruits.
Remember (him) in your mind again and again,
(and) your attachments to Maya will perish;
the imperishable Lord is with you;
O my mind, stay steeped in Ram's love.
In whose service all hunger is taken away,
in whose service Jam's messengers do not (even) look (your way),
in whose service great is your glory,
in whose service you become immortal;
whose servant suffers no penalty,
whose servant has no evil habit,
in whose register no account is called for:
serve him above all.
He who lacks nothing at all,
who, himself the One, is in countless forms,
by whose glance (of grace) one is happy for ever:
O my mind, serve him.
No one is clever (of himself), and no one a fool;
no one is weak, and no one a hero;
to whatever (God) attaches someone, to that he is attached;
O Nanak, he alone is (God's) servant who is so fortunate.
239.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Without Simran (life) is like the (long) life of a snake;
so live the Saakats, forgetting the Name.
One who has lived even an instant in Simran
(has, as it were, lived) millions of days, (and) has become steadfast for ever.
Without Simran the deeds one does are cursed;
like the crow's beak, (their) dwelling is in filth.
Without Simran (people) become like dogs in their deeds;
the Saakats are like a prostitute's son, who bears no (father's) name.
Without Simran (one) is like a horned ram;
the Saakats speak falsehood, (and their) faces are blackened.
Without Simran (one) is like a donkey;
the Saakats wander about in places of corruption.
Without Simran (one) is like a rabid dog;
the greedy Saakat knows no restraint.
Without Simran (one) is the slayer of his own soul;
the Saakat is low; he has no family and no caste.
The one to whom (God) has been gracious, (God) has joined to the Sat Sangat;
says Nanak, the Guru has carried the world across.
239.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By the Guru's word I have reached the supreme state;
the perfect Guru has kept my honour.
By the Guru's word I have meditated on the Name;
by the Guru's grace I have found a place (to rest).
By the Guru's word I hear (the Lord's praise), and utter (it) with my tongue;
by the Guru's grace, the ambrosial (Bani) has become my speech.
By the Guru's word my self-conceit is erased;
by the Guru's kindness great is my glory.
By the Guru's word my doubt is erased;
By the Guru's word I have seen God everywhere.
By the Guru's word I have practised Raj Jog;
in the Guru's company the whole world has swum across.
By the Guru's word my tasks are accomplished;
By the Guru's word I have found the treasure of the Name.
Whoever has placed his hope in my Guru,
the noose of Jam is cut for him.
By the Guru's word my fortune has awakened;
Nanak has met the Guru, the Supreme Lord.
239.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I remember that Guru with every breath;
the Guru is the very breath of my life; the True Guru is my capital.
Beholding the Guru's sight again and again, I live;
I wash the Guru's feet again and again, and drink (that water).
I bathe every day in the dust of the Guru's feet,
(and) wash away the filth of Haumai of birth after birth.
I wave the fan over that Guru,
(who) gave (me) his hand and saved (me) from the great fire.
I carry water in the house of that Guru
from whom (I) have come to know the state of the Indivisible (God).
I grind (the corn) every day in the house of that Guru,
by whose grace all enemies have (become) friends.
The Guru who has given me (the spirit's) life
has himself bought his humble servant as his own.
He himself has given (me) his love;
for ever and ever I bow to that Guru.
Strife, anguish, fears, doubt and pain are gone;
says Nanak, my Guru is all-powerful.
240.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Meet me, my Gobind; give me your Name.
Without the Name, cursed, cursed is (every other) attachment.
One who wears and eats without the Name
is like a dog putting its mouth into leftovers.
All the dealings carried on without the Name
are as vain as the adorning of a corpse.
One who forgets the Name and indulges in pleasures
finds no peace even in dreams; diseases (beset his) body.
One who abandons the Name and busies himself with other tasks
comes to ruin; all (his) shows are false.
One who does not join his mind in love with the Name
goes to hell, though he performs millions of rites.
One who has not worshipped the Lord's Name in his mind
is bound like a thief in the city of Jam.
Lakhs of pompous shows and a vast spread of things:
without the Name, (all this) display is false.
That servant alone takes the Lord's Name
to whom, O Nanak, (God) gives it in his grace.
240.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The One who stands by (me) at the beginning, in the middle and at the end:
that Friend my mind longs for.
Love for the Lord goes along with (one) for ever;
the merciful, perfect Being, present in all, cherishes (all).
He does not perish, nor does he leave (us) and go;
wherever I look, there he is pervading.
(God) is beautiful, accomplished, wise, the Giver of life;
brother, son, father and mother: God is (all these to me).
(He is) the prop of (my) life and breath, my wealth;
enshrining (him) in my heart, I have given (him) my love.
Gopal has cut away (my) noose of Maya;
looking on (me) with his glance of grace, he has made (me) his own.
Remembering (him) again and again, all ills are cut away;
meditation on (his) feet is the enjoyment of every comfort.
The perfect Being is ever new, ever young;
the Lord is within and without, with (us), our protector.
Says Nanak: (the devotee) has recognised the state of (union with) the Lord, Har Har;
(the Lord) has given the devotee the Name, which is everything.
240.3: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Countless have wandered searching, (but none) has found (your) limit;
they alone became devotees on whom (your) grace fell.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice to the Lord.
Hearing again and again that the road is fearsome, I was gripped by great fear;
I have looked to the shelter of the Sants: save (me).
O enchanting Beloved, incomparable, support of all,
bowing low again and again, I fall at the Guru's feet: (O Guru,) show (me the Lord).
I made friends of many, (but) it is to the One alone that I am a sacrifice;
all virtues are found in no one (else); the Lord's storehouses (alone) are full.
(Your) Name is repeated in all four directions; (those who repeat it) are made beautiful in peace.
I have sought your shelter; Nanak is a sacrifice (to you).
Stretching out his arm, the Guru has pulled (me) out of the well of attachment;
I have won (the game of) this life of boundless worth, never to lose again.
I have found (God), the treasure of all, whose story cannot be told;
in the Lord's court (I) am honoured, and walk swinging (my) arms, free of care.
Servant Nanak has found the priceless, boundless jewel (of the Name);
by serving the Guru, one crosses the terrifying world-ocean: this I proclaim aloud.
241.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Dye (your mind) in the love of Narayan, the Lord;
repeat (his Name) with your tongue, and ask for the one Lord alone.
Give up Haumai and, through the wisdom the Guru gives, worship (the Lord);
this is done, joining the Sangat, by one for whom grace was written from the Source.
Whatever is seen has gone along with no one;
the foolish Saakat clings to it and wastes away to death.
The Name of the Enchanter pervades (all) for ever;
among millions, only someone rare has found it, through the Guru.
Bow, bow in reverence to the Lord's Sants;
you will obtain the nine treasures and peace beyond measure.
May (my) eyes behold the holy ones;
sing in your heart of the treasure of the Name.
Give up lust, anger, greed and attachment;
(one who does) is spared both birth and death.
Pain and darkness have gone from the home (of the heart),
(since) the Guru has made divine wisdom firm (within), and the lamp is alight.
Whoever served (the Lord) has crossed to the far shore;
O servant Nanak, through the Guru the world crosses over.
241.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Uttering Har Har, Guru Guru, (my) doubts have gone;
my mind has found every comfort.
I was burning, ablaze; sprinkled with the Guru's sandalwood, I was cooled.
The darkness of ignorance is gone: the Guru's wisdom has shone forth.
The ocean of fire is deep; boarding the boat of the Sants, I have been carried across.
I had no (good) deeds, no righteousness, no purity; God took (me) by the arm and made (me) his own.
Destroyer of fear, dispeller of pain, is the Name of the Lord, the lover of devotion.
O Master of the masterless, compassionate to the humble, almighty, shelter of the Sants,
this is the prayer of one without virtue: grant (me) the sight of you, O Lord King.
Nanak is in your refuge, O Master; (your) servant has come to your door.
242.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One) takes delight in the pleasures of Maya; engrossed in them, the blind one understands nothing.
I amass, I earn: (so) the whole span of life has passed.
I am a hero, I am a chief; there is no one like me;
I am young, of good conduct, of noble family: so (one) grows proud in (his) mind.
As the one of fettered understanding stays entangled (in Maya), even while dying he does not forget (her).
Brothers, friends, kin and companions: to them, afterwards, (all he gathered) is handed over.
The desire the mind is attached to is the one that shows itself at the last.
Performing rites of purity with a mind full of self, (one) is held fast in these bonds.
O merciful Being, present in all, have mercy: Nanak is the slave of your slaves.
242.2: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Gauri Poorbi, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
For the young bride the night is full of pain; sleep does not come;
the soul-bride has grown frail, sighing for her Husband.
Sighing for her Spouse, the bride has wasted away: how might she see (him) with her eyes?
Adornment, sweet tastes, pleasures and fine food: all is false, of no account.
She who is drunk with youth as with wine is worn away by pride; milk once drawn does not come back to the teats.
O Nanak, the soul-bride meets (her Husband) only when she is brought to meet (him); without the Husband, sleep does not come.
Without her beloved Master, the young bride is forlorn.
How will she find peace without holding (him) to her heart?
Without the Husband the home is no home to dwell in; ask (your) friends and companions.
Without the Name there is no love or affection (for him); those who dwell in the True One live at ease.
With truth in the mind, and in contentment, comes the meeting with the Friend; through the Guru's teaching the Husband is known.
O Nanak, the soul-bride who does not let go of the Name merges in Sahaj through the Name.
Come together, my friends and companions; let us enjoy our Husband.
Asking the Guru, I shall write (to him) a message through the Shabad.
The Guru has shown the true Shabad; the self-willed (brides) repent.
The (mind) that kept running off stays steady once the True One is recognised.
The understanding of the True One is ever new; through the Shabad love stays ever fresh.
O Nanak, by (his) glance of grace the True One (is met) in Sahaj; meet (him), my friends and companions.
My wish is fulfilled: the Friend has come to my home.
Groom and bride have met, and the song of joy has been sung.
Singing the joyful song of (his) virtues, the young bride rejoices in love; her mind is full of eager delight.
The friends rejoice, the wicked are distressed; meditating on the True One, the true profit (is gained).
With palms joined, the soul-bride prays, drenched night and day in the relish (of his love).
O Nanak, Husband and bride delight together; my wish is fulfilled.
243.1: Raag Gauri, a Chhant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Hear me, O Husband, dear God: I am all alone in the forest (of this world).
How will (your bride) take heart without her Husband, O carefree Lord?
The bride cannot live without her Husband; the night is very hard (for her).
Sleep does not come; (your) love is dear (to me); hear my prayer.
Apart from the Beloved no one cares for (me); all alone, (the bride) cries out.
O Nanak, the soul-bride meets (her Husband) only when she is brought to meet (him); without the Beloved she suffers pain.
She whom the Husband has left: who can bring her to him?
She who has met (him) in the relish of love is made beautiful by the Shabad.
Made beautiful by the Shabad, she then gains honour; the lamp (of wisdom) lights up her body.
Listen, my friend and companion: she is at ease in the True One who cherishes the True One's virtues.
When the True Guru united her, the Husband delighted in her; through the Amrit Bani she blossomed.
O Nanak, the soul-bride enjoys her Husband only when she is pleasing to his mind.
Maya the enchantress has left her homeless; she who clings to falsehood is plundered by falsehood.
How can the noose at her neck be loosed without the most beloved Guru?
One who loves the Lord and reflects (on him) through the Shabad becomes his alone.
How can charity, alms and countless bathings wash away the filth within?
Without the Name no one is set free: not by stubborn will, not by curbing the senses, not by (living in) the wilderness.
O Nanak, the true home is recognised through the Shabad; what can (one caught in) duality know of the mansion?
Your Name is true, dear Lord; your Shabad is true, and reflection (on it).
Your mansion is true, dear Lord; true is the trade in the Name.
The trade in the Name is sweet; devotion is its profit, night and day.
Apart from it, no other merchandise is worth a thought; take the Name each and every moment.
The account is assayed, and (his) true glance of grace (falls); by (his) perfect grace (the Name) is obtained.
O Nanak, the Name is the supreme relish, and sweet; through the Perfect Guru the True One has been found.
243.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, Chhants, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace.
The soul-bride offers her prayer, cherishing the Lord's virtues;
she cannot live a moment, an instant, without her beloved Lord.
Without her beloved Lord she cannot live; (but) without the Guru (his) mansion is not found.
Whatever the Guru says, that should be done in full; (thus) the fire of craving is quenched.
The Lord alone is true; there is none but him; without service (to him), no peace is found.
O Nanak, the soul-bride meets (her Husband) only when she is brought to meet (him): she whom he himself unites.
The bride's night passes in ease when she fixes her mind on the Lord.
She serves the True Guru with love, and sheds self-conceit from within.
Shedding self-conceit from within, she sings the Lord's praises; night and day her love (for him) holds.
Listen, my friend and companion, dear to my heart: merge in the Guru's Shabad.
When she cherishes the Lord's virtues, she is dear to her Husband; she has set her love on the Name alone.
O Nanak, the soul-bride is dear to her Husband, the Lord's Name a garland at her neck.
Without her beloved Husband the bride is all alone;
she is robbed through the love of another, without the Guru's mighty Shabad.
Without the beloved Shabad, who can carry (her) across the ocean so hard to cross? Attachment to Maya has led her astray.
When falsehood ruined her, her Husband cast her off; that bride does not reach (his) mansion.
(She who is) dyed in the Guru's Shabad, absorbed in Sahaj, stays merged (in him) night and day.
O Nanak, the bride who is ever dyed in (his) love is united (with him) by the dear Lord himself.
One meets (him) only when the Lord brings (one) to meet; who but the Lord can unite?
Without one's own beloved Guru, who can dispel doubt?
The Guru dispels doubt; in this way, O mother, (he) is met, and then the soul-bride is at peace.
Without service to the Guru, there is pitch darkness; without the Guru the path is not found.
The bride dyed in (his) love, absorbed in Sahaj, reflects (on him) through the Guru's Shabad.
O Nanak, through love for the beloved Guru, the bride has found the Lord as her Groom.
244.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without my Husband I am utterly forlorn; O my mother, how can I live without him?
Sleep will not come without the Husband, and no garment sits well on my body.
A garment looks fair on the body when (she) pleases her Husband; through the Guru's teaching the mind is fixed (on him).
When she serves the True Guru she is a happy wife for ever; it is in the Guru's embrace that one is absorbed.
Through the Guru's Shabad comes union, and then I enjoy my Husband; the Name is the (true) profit in the world.
O Nanak, the soul-bride is dear to her Husband when she cherishes the Lord's virtues.
The soul-bride enjoys delight with her own Beloved.
Day and night she is dyed in (his) love, and reflects on the Guru's Shabad.
She reflects on the Guru's Shabad and kills Haumai; in this way, (friends,) meet the Beloved.
That bride is a happy wife, ever dyed in (his) love, in love with the True Name.
Staying joined to one's own Guru, one lays hold of the amrit (of the Name), and she kills duality and casts it out.
O Nanak, the bride has found the Lord as her Groom, and has forgotten all her sorrows.
The bride strays from her Husband, in love with attachment to Maya.
False herself, she clings to the false; she who clings to falsehood is plundered by falsehood.
(If) she casts out falsehood and holds to the Guru's teaching, she does not gamble her life away.
She serves the Guru's Shabad, merges in the True One, and kills Haumai within.
She enshrines the Lord's Name in her heart: such is the adornment she makes.
O Nanak, the bride whose support is the True Name stays merged in Sahaj.
Meet me, my dear Beloved; without you I am utterly forlorn.
Sleep does not come to my eyes; neither food nor water pleases me.
Water and food do not please; one dies in sighs; without the Husband how can peace be found?
I make my prayer before the Guru: if it pleases the Guru, may he unite me (with the Lord) in whatever way he may be met.
The Giver of peace himself unites (her with him); he himself has come home and met (her).
