Those within whom is the treasure of the Lord's Name: the Master has brought their affairs to fulfilment.
Their dependence on people is ended; the Lord God has taken their side and sits beside them.
When the Creator is on (their) side, everyone is on (their) side; all who look on them acclaim them.
Bankers and emperors are all of the Lord's making; all come and make supplication to the Lord's servant.
Great is the glory of the Perfect Guru: serving the great Lord, (his servant) has found peace beyond weighing.
The Perfect Guru has given the gift of the Lord('s Name), which never fails; the Lord bestows it every day, and it grows ever greater.
Any slanderer who cannot bear to see (this) glory, the Creator himself has consumed.
Servant Nanak speaks the virtues of the Creator, who has always kept his devotees safe.
305.2: (O Lord,) you are the Master, beyond reach and merciful, the great Giver, the Wise One.
I see no other as great as you; you alone, the accomplished one, are pleasing to my mind.
Attachment and family, all that is seen, is bound to pass; (it is all) coming and going.
Those who set their minds anywhere but on the True One are false, and their pride is false.
O Nanak, meditate on the True One; without the True One the ignorant burn and burn away to death.
305.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
First (the manmukh) gives (the Guru) no regard; what he says afterwards is of no use.
The poor manmukh wanders, caught halfway; how can he find peace by talk?
One within whom there is no love for the True Guru comes in falsehood and goes in falsehood.
If my Lord God, the Creator, shows grace, then (one) sees the True Guru as the Supreme Lord.
Then he drinks the Amrit, the Guru's Shabad, and puts an end to all fret, worry and doubt.
He stays in bliss for ever, day and night; O servant Nanak, he sings the Lord's virtues night and day.
305.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
One known as a Sikh of the Guru, the True Guru, rises early and meditates on the Lord's Name.
He makes the effort, early in the hours before dawn; he bathes, and dips in the pool of Amrit.
By the Guru's teaching he chants the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and all his sins, misdeeds and faults are washed away.
Then, as the day rises, he sings Gurbani; sitting down and rising up, he meditates on the Lord's Name.
Whoever, with every breath and every morsel, meditates on my Lord, Har Har: that Gursikh pleases the Guru's mind.
The one to whom my Master is merciful: to that Gursikh the Guru imparts his teaching.
Servant Nanak begs for the dust of that Gursikh's feet, who repeats the Naam himself and has others repeat it.
306.1: (O Lord,) those who meditate on you, the True One, are rare, and few.
Those who worship the One with mind and heart: countless millions eat by their blessing.
All (creation) meditates on you, (but) those alone are accepted whom the Master wants.
Those who eat and clothe themselves without serving the True Guru are lepers: they die, and having died are born (again).
To one's face they speak sweetly, but behind one's back they spit out poison mixed in their mouths.
The false at heart the Master has cut off (from himself).
306.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
A blue-black blanket full of dirt and lice: that renegade (one turned away from the Guru) put it on the renegade (his servant).
No one in the world lets him sit near; having fallen in filth, the manmukh came back smeared with still more dirt.
Made a renegade, he was sent to slander others and tell tales; there too the faces of both renegades were blackened.
At once it was heard all over the world, O brother, that the renegade and his servant were beaten with shoes, and, dazed, he got up and came home.
After that the renegade was not allowed to mix in gatherings or among his in-laws; then his wife and his niece brought him and laid him in the house again.
Both this world and the next are lost (to him); he cries out every day, hungry and thirsty.
Blessed, blessed is the Master, the Creator, the Being, who himself sat and had true justice done.
Whoever slanders the Perfect True Guru, the True One has struck down and consumed.
This word was spoken by the one who brought the whole world into being.
306.3: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
One whose master is naked and hungry: how can that servant eat his fill?
What is in the master's house comes into the servant's hands; what is not there, where can he get it?
One served who then demands an account: that service is hard.
Says Nanak, serve the Lord, the Guru, whose sight bears fruit; then no one asks for an account.
306.4: O Nanak, the Sants reflect, and the four Vedas declare,
that the words the devotees speak with their mouths come to pass.
This is plainly seen in the world, and all people hear (of it).
Foolish men who quarrel with the Sants find no peace.
The (Sants) long for their good, (but) they burn in their pride.
What can the wretches do, when their lot is evil from the first?
Those struck down by the Supreme Lord belong to no one.
They bear enmity to those who bear none, and by the justice of Dharam they burn.
All whom the Sant has cursed go wandering about.
When the tree is cut at the root, its branches wither.
306.5: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Guru meditates on the Lord within; great is (his) glory.
The Perfect One, well pleased, has given it to the True Guru; it does not lessen by a sesame seed for anyone's lessening.
The True Master is on the True Guru's side; so all the world may fret and fret itself to death.
The Lord, the Creator, makes the slanderers' faces black, and has himself increased (the Guru's) glory.
The more the slanderers slander, the more (this glory) grows, day after day.
O servant Nanak, (the Guru) has worshipped the Lord, and the Lord has brought all (the world) and laid it at (his) feet.
307.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Whoever keeps a grudge against the True Guru has lost all of this world and the next.
Every day he gnashes his teeth and foams at the mouth; fretting and fuming, he withers and falls.
Every day he schemes for Maya and wealth, (but) even the wealth he had before has flown away.
What can he earn, and what can he enjoy, within whom anxiety and pain have settled?
One who stirs up enmity against the one who bears none has taken the sin of the whole world on his head.
There is no shelter for him, here or hereafter, who has slander within and (the sweetness of) a mango in his mouth.
If he lays his hand on gold, it turns to dust.
If he comes back to the Guru's refuge, his past faults are forgiven.
O servant Nanak, (whoever) has meditated on the Naam night and day: remembering the Lord, his sins and misdeeds are gone.
307.2: (O Lord,) you alone are the True One, you are Truth; you are above all, you are the support (of all).
Those who meditate on you, the True One, and serve the True One, take pride in you, O True One.
Truth is within them, their faces are bright; they speak the Truth, and you, O True One, are their strength.
They are devotees who have praised (you) through the Guru; the true Shabad is their insignia.
Those who serve the True One in truth: to them I am ever a sacrifice.
307.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those struck down from the very first by the Perfect True Guru, those same the True Guru has now struck down.
However much one may long to unite them (with the Guru), the Creator does not let them meet.
They find no shelter in the Sat Sangat; the Guru has weighed this and (declared it) in the Sangat.
Whoever goes and meets them now, cruel Jam strikes him down.
Those whom Guru Baba (Guru Nanak Dev Ji) rebuked stayed rebuked; Guru Angad (Dev Ji) declared them false.
The Guru of the third generation (Guru Amar Das Ji) reflected: what lies in the hands of these poor wretches?
(The Guru) who installed the Guru of the fourth generation (Guru Ram Das Ji) carried all the slanderers and the wicked across.
Whoever, son or Sikh, serves the True Guru has all his affairs set right.
He will obtain whatever fruit he wishes, sons, riches and prosperity; (the Guru) leads him to union (with God), and the Lord carries him across.
All treasures are in the True Guru, who keeps the Lord enshrined in his heart.
He alone finds the Perfect True Guru on whose forehead (this) writ is written.
Servant Nanak begs for the dust of those Gursikhs' feet, who are beloved friends.
308.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those whom (God) himself grants glory: he himself also brings the world and lays it at their feet.
We would have cause to fear if we did anything of ourselves; it is the Creator who is increasing his own power in everything.
See, O brother: this is the arena of the Lord, the true Beloved, who by his own might has brought all to bow down.
The Lord, the Master, protects his devotees, and blackens the faces of the slanderers and the wicked.
The True Guru's glory grows ever greater; the Lord himself every day has (him) sing (his) praise and worship (him).
Repeat the Naam night and day, O Gursikhs; the Lord, the Creator, will make the True Guru dwell in (the home of your heart).
Know the True Guru's Bani to be true, true indeed, O Gursikhs; the Lord, the Creator, himself brings it forth from (the Guru's) mouth.
The beloved Lord makes the Gursikhs' faces bright, and has the Guru acclaimed everywhere in the world.
Servant Nanak is the Lord's slave; the Lord himself keeps the honour of his slaves.
308.2: (O Lord,) you yourself are the True Master, O our true Banker.
O God, make the true capital, the Naam, firm in us; (we are) your traders.
(We) serve the True One, buy the merchandise of Truth, and tell of (your) matchless virtues.
Those who live in the spirit of servants have met (you), adorned by the Guru's Shabad.
You are the True Master, the Unseen; through the Guru's Shabad you are made known.
308.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
One within whom is envy of others never comes to good.
No one heeds what he says; he is ever standing in a wilderness, crying out.
One within whom is backbiting comes to be known as a backbiter; all he has ever done is lost.
Every day he tells untrue tales against others; his face is blackened, and he cannot show it.
In Kalyug the body is the field of deeds; as one sows, so one eats.
Judgement is not passed on words; whoever eats poison dies at once.
O brother, see the true justice of the Creator: as one does, so one receives.
(God) has given servant Nanak full understanding; he tells the things of the Lord's court.
308.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those who broke away from the Guru even while he was present before their eyes find no shelter at (the Lord's) door.
Whoever goes and meets those slanderers (shares their lot): their faces are pale, and spit upon spit falls on their faces.
Those cursed by the True Guru are cursed by the whole world; they ever stumble about, lost.
Those who have disowned their own Guru wander about, wailing aloud.
Their hunger never leaves them; they ever cry out: hunger, hunger.
No one listens to what they say; day after day they die in dread upon dread.
They cannot bear to see the True Guru's greatness; for them there is no place, here or hereafter.
Those who go and join the ones struck down by the True Guru lose whatever honour they had left.
Cursed by the Guru, they are lepers already; whoever meets such a one, leprosy breaks out on him too.
O Lord, let (me) not even see those who fix their minds on the love of another.
The Creator himself wrote (this) from the start and set it down; against it there is no remedy.
O servant Nanak, worship the Name in adoration; none can reach up to it.
Great is the greatness of the Name; it rises ever higher, growing more each day.
309.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The one whom the Guru, while still present, sat and anointed with the tilak (as Guru): that servant's greatness has become great.
The whole world bows before him and falls at his feet; his praise has spread through all the world.
Continents and universes bow to him; the one on whose forehead the perfect Guru has placed his hand becomes perfect.
The Guru's greatness rises ever higher, growing more each day; none can reach up to it.
The Lord, the Creator, himself sat and installed servant Nanak (as Guru); that God himself keeps (his) honour.
309.2: The body is a boundless fortress, with market streets within.
One who trades (there) through the Guru gathers in the merchandise of the Lord.
(Here) one deals in the treasure of the Lord's Name: diamonds and corals.
Those who search for this wealth anywhere outside the body are fools and ghouls.
In doubt they are made to wander through the wilds, as the deer searches the bushes (for the musk within itself).
309.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Whoever slanders the perfect True Guru comes to grief in the world.
Terrible hell is a well of pain; he is seized and cast into it.
No one hears his cries and wails; in anguish upon anguish he weeps.
He has lost this world and the next entirely, and squandered profit and capital alike.
Making him an oil-presser's ox, God yokes him (to the press) as each morning comes.
The Lord ever sees and hears everything; nothing is hidden from him.
As one sows, so one reaps: whatever each has sown before.
The one on whom God bestows his grace washes the True Guru's feet.
Following the Guru, the True Guru, he crosses over, as iron (floats across) joined to wood.
O servant Nanak, meditate on the Name; repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har: in the Name is peace.
309.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Greatly fortunate are the happy wives whom the Lord King has met through the Guru.
The light within (them) shines forth; O Nanak, they merge in the Name.
309.5: This whole body is (the dwelling of) dharma, within which is the light of the True One.
Secret jewels lie hidden in it; some rare Gurmukh, a servant (of the Lord), digs them out.
When he recognises the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram) everywhere, then (he sees) the One alone pervading all, through and through like warp and weft.
He has seen the One, put his faith in the One, and heard with his ears of the One alone.
O servant Nanak, praise the Name: (this) is your true service of the True One.
310.1: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
All delights are in the hearts of those in whose minds the Lord has come to dwell.
In the Lord's court their faces shine; all go to see them.
No fear at all remains for those who have meditated on the Name of the Fearless One.
They alone have served the exalted Lord in whose lot it was written from the start.
Those in whose minds the Lord has come to dwell are robed in honour in the Lord's court.
They themselves cross over with all their families, and they set the whole world free in their wake.
O Lord, unite servant Nanak with (such) servants of yours, beholding whom again and again we live.
310.2: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
That ground has turned green where my True Guru came and sat.
Those beings have turned green who went and saw my True Guru.
Blessed, blessed the father, blessed, blessed the family, blessed, blessed the mother who gave birth to the Guru, O mother.
Blessed, blessed is the Guru, who worshipped the Name: he crossed over himself, and those who saw him he sets free as well.
O Lord, show mercy and bring (me) to the True Guru; let servant Nanak wash (his) feet.
310.3: The True Guru is true, ever true, and immortal, who has enshrined the Lord within his heart.
The True Guru is the Being, true, ever true, who has killed the poison of lust and anger.
When I saw the perfect True Guru, my mind within found its support.
I am a sacrifice to my Guru; for ever and ever I give myself up to him.
The Gurmukh has won (the game of life), and the manmukh has lost.
310.4: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The one whom (God) in his mercy has united with the True Guru meditates on the Name with his mouth, through the Guru.
He does whatever is pleasing to the True Guru; the perfect Guru settles (the Name) in the home of his heart.
Those within whom is the treasure of the Name: (the Guru) takes away all their fear.
Those whom the Lord himself stands by to protect: how many others wear themselves out, toiling (against them), and are gone.
O servant Nanak, meditate on the Name; the Lord will set (you) free here and hereafter.
310.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Gursikhs' minds delight in the greatness of the Guru, the True Guru.
O Lord, you keep the True Guru's honour; (so his greatness) rises ever higher, growing more each day.
The Guru, the True Guru, holds the Supreme Lord in his mind; the Supreme Lord (himself) delivers (him).
The Lord is the might and mainstay of the Guru, the True Guru; he has brought all and made them bow (before the Guru).
Those who looked upon my True Guru with love: all their sins (the Guru) has taken away.
In the Lord's court their faces shine, and they have won great honour.
Servant Nanak asks for the dust (of the feet) of those who are the Guru's Sikhs, my brothers.
310.6: Let me speak his praise and extol (him); his praise is true, true is the greatness of the True One.
Let me praise the True One; the True One is worthy of praise; no one has found the True One's worth.
Those who have tasted the essence, true, ever true, remain fulfilled and satisfied.
They alone know this essence of the Lord, like a mute who has eaten sweets (and cannot tell of it).
Those who served the Lord God through the perfect Guru: in their minds the music of rejoicing has sounded.
311.1: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those who have an abscess within, they alone know its stabbing pains.
(So) they alone know the pang of separation from the Lord (who feel it); I am ever a sacrifice, a sacrifice to them.
O Lord, unite (me with) my friend, the Being (the Guru); for them let my head roll beneath (their feet).
The Sikhs who carry out the Guru's work: I am the slave of their slaves.
Those dyed in the deep crimson of the Lord's love: their robe is soaked in the Lord's love.
(O Lord,) in your mercy unite Nanak with the Guru; he has sold his head to him at a price.
311.2: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The body is filled with faults; O Sants, how can it become pure?
Through the Guru virtues are bought, (and so one) washes out the filth of Haumai.
Those who trade in Truth with love: (theirs) is a true bargain.
There is no loss in it at all; the profit is that they become pleasing to the Lord.
O Nanak, they alone have traded in Truth who receive it as was written for them from the start.
311.3: Let me praise the True One, who is worthy of praise, the Being, true, ever true, and apart from all.
Let me serve the True One, and let the True One dwell in (my) mind; the Lord, true, ever true, is the protector (of all).
Those who worshipped the True One, ever true, have gone and merged with the True One.
Those who did not serve the True One, ever true, are manmukhs, fools and ghouls.
They babble nonsense from their mouths, like drunkards who have drunk wine.
311.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through Raag Gauri (the soul-bride) is of fine qualities only if she keeps her Master in her mind;
(if) she walks in the will of the True Guru, and makes this her adornment.
The true Shabad is (her) Husband; she enjoys (his love) for ever and ever.
As boiled madder yields a deep colour, so she gives her life to the True One.
She is dyed through and through in deep crimson; her love is bound to the True One.
Falsehood and fraud do not stay hidden, though you wrap falsehood in gilding.
(The false) make false boasts; their love is bound to what is false.
O Nanak, (the Lord) himself is the True One; he himself casts his glance of grace.
311.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
In the Sat Sangat is the praise of the Lord; (there) the beloved ones meet in the Saadh's company.
Blessed are those men, those mortals, (the Lord's) servants, who teach for the good of others.
They make the Lord's Name firm (in others), they make (them) hear the Lord's Name; through the Lord's Name they have carried the world across.
Everyone longs to see the Guru; the nine regions of the world bow to him.
You yourself have placed yourself within the True Guru, and you yourself have adorned the Guru.
You yourself worship the True Guru, and have (others) worship him, O Creator.
If anyone breaks away from the True Guru, his face is blackened, and Jam has struck him down.
For him there is no shelter, here or hereafter; this the Gursikhs have weighed in their minds.
Those who met the True Guru, they alone have been saved, who cherished the Name in their hearts.
O Gursikhs, sons of servant Nanak, repeat (the Name of) the Lord: the Lord has carried (the world) across.
312.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Haumai has led the world astray: (it is caught in) evil-mindedness, Maya and vice.
If the True Guru is met, then comes (God's) glance of grace; the manmukhs are in blind darkness.
O Nanak, he himself unites with himself the one whom he attaches in love to the Shabad.
312.2: True is the praise of the True One; that one alone sings it whose inner self is soaked (in love).
Those who worshipped the One with one-pointed mind: their body never wastes away.
Blessed, blessed are those beings, and praise be to them, who drink the true nectar with the tongue.
Those whose minds love the True One, ever true, are accepted in the true court.
Blessed, blessed is the life of the truthful; the True One makes their faces bright.
312.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Saakats go and bow before the Guru, but they are counterfeit at heart, false through and through.
When the Guru says: Rise, my brothers, they squeeze in (among the Sikhs) and sit down like cranes.
The True Guru is at work within the Gursikhs; at the sifting, (the false) are picked out and put out.
Seated now in front, now behind, they hide their faces; but the counterfeit do not mingle (with the true).
Their fodder is not to be found there; like sheep they go (elsewhere) and find falsehood.
Though one longs to feed a Saakat (with good food), he brings up poison, spewing it from his mouth.
O Lord, let (me) never keep company with the Saakat: such are struck down by the Creator.
The one whose play this is makes it and watches it; servant Nanak cherishes the Name.
312.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The True Guru is the inaccessible Being, who has enshrined the Lord within his heart.
No one can reach up to the True Guru, on whose side is the Creator.
The True Guru's sword and armour are devotion to the Lord, with which he has struck down Death, the thorn, and driven it away.
The True Guru's protector is the Lord himself; all who follow the True Guru the Lord has saved.
Whoever wishes ill to the perfect True Guru is struck down by the Maker himself.
This is how it comes to pass in the court of the True Lord; servant Nanak has reflected on the Inaccessible One.
312.5: Those who have worshipped the True One even in their sleep utter the True One when they rise.
Such people are known to be rare in the world, who dwell on the True One through the Guru.
I am a sacrifice to those who take the True One's Name night and day.
Those whose minds and bodies love the True One reach the true court.
Servant Nanak utters the true Name: the True One, ever true, is new for ever.
312.6: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Asleep or awake, it is all one: the Gurmukhs are accepted.
Those who do not forget (God) with any breath or morsel are perfect and foremost among men.
By (God's) grace the True Guru is found, and the mind stays fixed (on God) night and day.
May I stay joined in their company, and win honour in (the Lord's) court.
As they lie down to sleep they utter Waah Waah (praise), and as they rise they praise him too.
O Nanak, bright are the faces of those who rise each day and cherish (the Lord in their hearts).
313.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
If one serves one's own True Guru, the infinite Naam is obtained.
The Lord, the Giver, grants (the Name as) his gift, and pulls out those who are drowning in the terrible world-ocean.
Blessed, blessed are those bankers who trade with (the capital of) the Name.
The Sikhs come (to the Guru) as traders, and (the Guru), through the Shabad, carries them across.
O servant Nanak, those on whom (God's) grace has fallen have served the Creator.
313.2: The true servants and devotees of the True One are those who have worshipped the True One, ever true.
Those who searched and sought through the Guru found the True One within themselves.
The Master is true; those who served the True One have struck down Death, the thorn, and brought it under control.
The True One, ever true, is greater than all; those who serve the True One are merged in the True One.
True praise be to the True One; serving the True One, ever true, (a life) bears fruit.
313.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The manmukh is a fool; empty of the Name, he wanders astray.
Without the Guru his mind does not hold still, and again and again he falls into births.
When the Lord God himself is merciful, the True Guru comes and meets (him).
O servant Nanak, praise the Name, and the pain of birth and death will go.
313.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
I praise my Guru in many ways, with love and with all my heart.
(My) mind is dyed in (the love of) the True Guru; (the Guru) has shaped it well and kept it so.
(My) tongue is never sated with praising, the mind fixed on the Lord, the Beloved.
O Nanak, in the mind is a hunger for the Name; the mind is satisfied only when it tastes the Lord's nectar.
313.5: The True One, ever true, who made the days and the nights, is known through his creation.
I praise that True One for ever and ever; true are the glories of the True One.
The True One is worthy of praise, and true is (his) praise; no one has found the worth of the True One.
When the perfect True Guru was met, then (those glories) came plainly into view.
Those who praised the True One through the Guru have lost all their hungers.
313.6: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Searching and searching my mind and body, I have sought out and found that God.
I found the Guru, the go-between, who joined me to the Lord God.
313.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who holds Maya (in his heart) is utterly blind and deaf.
He does not hear the Shabad, but raises a great noise and clamour.
The Gurmukh is known by this: he fixes his loving attention on the Shabad.
Hearing the Lord's Name, he believes in it, and merges in the Lord's Name.
Whatever pleases him, that (the creature) does, as he is made to do.
O Nanak, the creature sounds (like an instrument) as (God) plays it.
314.1: You, O Creator, know everything that goes on within all beings.
You, the Creator, are yourself beyond all reckoning; the whole world is caught in reckoning.
All that happens is of your doing; all (creation) is of your making.
You, the One, are at work in every heart; O True Master, (all this is your) wondrous play.
Those who meet the True Guru meet the Lord; no one can turn them back (from him).
314.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Let us hold this mind firm, and through the Guru fix our consciousness (on the Lord).
Why should we forget (him) with any breath or morsel, sitting or rising, each day?
(Then) the worry of death and life is gone, and this soul (comes) into the power of the Lord God.
(O God,) keep (me) as it pleases you; grant servant Nanak the Name.
314.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The proud manmukh does not know the mansion (of the True Guru); one moment he is forward, the next he holds back.
Though he is called again and again, he does not come to (the Guru's) mansion; how then can he succeed in (the Lord's) court?
Rare is the one who knows the True Guru's mansion, who stands always with palms joined.
O Nanak, (the one on whom) my Lord shows his grace, he turns (that one) back (to himself).
314.4: That service alone bears fruit by which the True Guru's mind is pleased.
Once the True Guru's mind was pleased, sins and stains were shattered.
The teaching the True Guru gave, the Sikhs heard with their own ears.
Those who accepted the True Guru's will took on a colour four times as deep.
This is the singular way of the Gurmukhs: hearing the Guru's teaching, (their) mind is drenched (in love).
314.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Whoever has slandered his own Guru has neither place nor resting place.
Both this world and the next are lost to him; in (the Lord's) court there is no place (for him).
That moment does not come to hand again, when (such people) might fall at the True Guru's feet.
If one goes astray in a grudge against the True Guru, (life) passes in sorrow upon sorrow.
The True Guru, the Being, is without enmity; he himself attaches (to his feet) whomever (he will).
O Nanak, those to whom (God) has granted the sight (of the Guru), he sets free in (his) court.
314.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh is ignorant, evil-minded and proud.
Anger is within him, and he has gambled away his understanding.
He practises falsehood, deceit and sin.
What can he hear, and what is he to tell others?
Blind and deaf, he loses (the way) and falls into the wilderness.
The blind manmukh keeps coming and going.
Without meeting the True Guru he is not accepted (at the Lord's door).
O Nanak, he acts out what was written before (by his past deeds).
314.7: Those whose hearts are hard do not sit near the True Guru.
Truth is at work there, and (so) the minds of the false are cheerless.
With twists and tricks they pass the time (there), then go and sit again with the false.
Falsehood does not blend with the true: let anyone judge it in the mind and see.
The false go and join the false, and the truthful Sikhs sit by the True Guru.
315.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The slanderers who were left, (God) has struck down, himself taking the task in hand.
O Nanak, (God), the helper of the Sants, is at work everywhere, plain to see.
315.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who have strayed from the Root from the very start: where can they lay hold?
O Nanak, they are struck down by him who is the Cause of creation, all-powerful.
315.3: Pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
They set out at night with nooses, but God knows (these) mortals.
Hidden in secret places, they eye the women of others.
They break in at places hard to reach, and enjoy wine, taking it for sweet.
By their own deeds, each one, they themselves come to regret.
Azrail, the angel (of death), crushes (them) like sesame seeds in the oil-press.
315.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who are servants of the True King, they alone are accepted.
O Nanak, those who serve another (than him), those ignorant ones burn and burn away and die.
315.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The writ God has written from the beginning cannot be erased.
O Nanak, the Lord's Name is (the true) wealth and merchandise: meditate on it always.
315.6: Pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one whom Narayan himself has thrust away: where can he set his foot?
He commits countless sins, and every day tastes nothing but poison.
Slandering, he has wasted away and died; he burns within his own body.
He is struck down by the True Master: who can save him?
Nanak is in the refuge of the one who is the unseen Being.
315.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Terrible hells and many heavy sorrows: (this) is the abode of the ungrateful.
O Nanak, that God has struck them down; they die as ones untrue to their salt.
315.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) has made every medicine, but for the slanderer there is no cure.
O Nanak, (God) himself has led them astray; wasting away, they fall into birth after birth.
315.9: Pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The perfect True Guru, well pleased, has given the wealth of the Lord, true and inexhaustible.
All anxieties are erased, and the fear of Jam is gone.
Lust, anger and (other) evils are broken off in the company of the Saadh.
Those who serve another than the True One will die helpless, like a fledgling (fallen from the nest).
The Guru has blessed Nanak, and (he is) joined to the Name.
315.10: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
He is no ascetic who is greedy within and roams after Maya each day, a leper.
When first invited, he would not take the alms offered with respect; afterwards, regretting it, the ascetic brought his son and seated him in (the gathering).
All the elders began to laugh: the ascetic has been worn away by a wave of greed.
Where he sees little wealth, the ascetic will not go near; on seeing much wealth, the ascetic gave up his faith.
O brother, this is no ascetic but a crane (a hypocrite): so the holy people have judged, sitting together.
The ascetic slanders the true man and busies himself with the praise of the world; for this fault the Master has struck the ascetic down.
See the fruit the ascetic has reaped for slandering the great beings: all the ascetic's labour is lost.
Sitting outside among the elders, he has himself called an ascetic; sitting inside, the ascetic commits sins; the Lord has laid bare (his) hidden sin and shown it to the elders.
Dharam Raj has told Jam's servants: Take this ascetic and throw him where the worst of all murderers are.
And let none of you have any dealings with this ascetic again: he has been cursed by the True Guru.
What took place at the Lord's door, Nanak has told aloud; he alone understands it whom the Master has adorned.
316.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord's devotees have worshipped the Lord and (sung) the Lord's greatness.
The devotees sing the Lord's Kirtan every day; the Lord's Name gives peace.
(He) has granted the Lord's devotees the glory of the Name for ever, (and it) rises ever higher, growing more each day.
(He) has seated the Lord's devotees steady in their own home, (and so) has kept his own honour.
The Lord will call the slanderers to account, and give them heavy punishment.
As the slanderers act in their own hearts, such is the fruit they receive.
What is done in secret surely comes to light, even if one does it sitting beneath the earth.
Servant Nanak has blossomed, seeing the Lord's greatness.
316.2: Pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord himself guards his devotees; what can a sinner do (to them)?
The foolish proud take pride, and die from the poison (of pride) they have eaten.
Their few short days run out, as a ripe crop is reaped.
As are the deeds they do, so are they called.
Servant Nanak's Master is great; he is the Lord of all.
316.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The manmukhs have strayed from the Root (God) itself; within them are craving, greed and pride.
Their time passes night and day in quarrels; they do not reflect through the Shabad.
The Creator has robbed them of all sense and understanding; all they speak is corrupt.
No gift whatever satisfies them; within them is great thirst, ignorance and darkness.
O Nanak, it is better to break with the manmukhs, whose love is attachment to Maya.
316.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those within whom is the love of another: in them love (for God) does not arise through the Guru.
Such a one comes and goes, made to wander (through births); not even in a dream does he know any peace.
He practises falsehood and speaks falsehood; clinging to falsehood, he becomes false himself.
Attachment to Maya is nothing but pain; in pain he perishes, and over his pain he weeps.
O Nanak, the chase after Maya and loving absorption (in God) cannot be joined, however much anyone may wish it.
Those in whose treasury merit has been laid up find peace through the Guru's Shabad.
316.5: Pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the Sants and the silent sages reflect, and the four Vedas declare,
that the words the devotees speak with their mouths come to pass.
They are seen openly in the world; all people hear (of them).
Foolish men who quarrel with the Sants find no peace.
The (Sants) long for their good, (but) they burn in their pride.
What can the wretches do, when their lot is evil from the first?
Those struck down by the Supreme Lord belong to no one.
They bear enmity to those who bear none, and by the justice of Dharam they burn.
All whom the Sant has cursed go wandering about.
When the tree is cut at the root, its branches wither.
317.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the Guru has firmly implanted (in the heart) the Name of the Lord, who has the power to break and to make.
O friend, if you keep God ever in mind, all (your) pain is gone.
317.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(As) a hungry man (begging) heeds no shame, disgrace or harsh word,
(so) Nanak begs for the Lord's Name: (O Lord,) in your mercy, grant the union (with you).
317.3: As are the deeds one does, such is the fruit they bear.
One who chews hot, hard iron finds it stuck in his throat.
Because of his deeds, the messenger (of Death) put a halter on his neck and drove him off.
Not one of his hopes was fulfilled; he was forever stealing others' filth (by slandering them).
The ingrate does not acknowledge the good done (to him); (so) he wanders through the births.
All his supports gave out, and he was snatched away from the earth.
He would not let the strife die down, so the Creator took him away.
All who act in ego wither and fall to the ground.
317.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through the Guru, one comes to have knowledge and a discerning intellect;
he sings the Lord's praises, and strings (them) into a garland for his heart.
He is pure, and makes (others) pure, and is of the highest understanding.
Whoever meets him, he carries across (the world-ocean).
Within him the fragrance of the Lord's Name abides.
At the Lord's door he is honoured, and his words are most sublime.
Whoever hears (them) is filled with delight.
O Nanak, meeting the True Guru, (he) has gained the Naam, his wealth and riches.
317.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The secret of the True Guru's heart cannot be known, what it is that pleases the perfect True Guru.
The True Guru is at work within the Gursikhs; whoever longs (to serve) the Sikhs comes into the Guru's favour.
What the True Guru says, that work (the Gursikhs) do, and that Jap (repetition of the Name) they practise; the True One accepts the toil of the Gursikhs.
One who wants work done by the Gursikhs without the True Guru's command: no Gursikh comes near him again.
If someone toils with his heart in it before the Guru, the True Guru, the Gursikh does service before him.
One who comes in deceit and rises to leave in deceit: no Gursikh ever goes near him.
Nanak speaks and proclaims (this) divine reflection: whoever has work done (by the Sikhs) without the True Guru's mind consenting, that creature suffers great pain.
317.6: (O God,) you are the True Master, exceedingly great; O greatest of the great, you alone are as great as you.
The one you unite (with you) meets you; you yourself forgive (him), setting his account aside.
The one you yourself unite serves the True Guru with his mind firmly fixed.
You are the True Master, you are the Eternal One; soul, body, skin and bones, all is yours.
Keep (me) as it pleases you, O True One; O greatest of the great, in Nanak's mind is hope in you alone.
318.1: Gauri ki Vaar: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji); to be sung to the tune of the vaar of Rai Kamaldi Mojdi.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one who repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har: his coming (into the world) is approved.
I am a sacrifice to that one who has worshipped God, who is beyond all desire.
His pain of birth and death is cut away, (for) he has met the Lord, the all-knowing Being.
O servant Nanak, in the company of the Sants he crosses the (world-) ocean; the True One is (his) strength.
318.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If, at the rising of the day, (a holy) guest were to come to my house,
I would wash his feet; he would be ever dear to my mind and body.
(Such a guest) would hear the Naam, gather the Naam, and keep himself attuned to the Naam alone.
(Through him my) home and wealth would all be made pure, and (I too) would sing the Lord's praises.
O Nanak, (such) a trader in the Lord's Name I find only by great good fortune.
318.3: (O God,) whatever pleases you is good; your will is true (and unfailing).
You, the One, are at work in all; you are contained in all.
You pervade every place and every space between; within (all) beings (you alone) are known.
Joining the Saadh Sangat, and accepting the True One's will, (he) is found.
Nanak has come to God's refuge, and is ever and ever a sacrifice (to him).
318.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If you have any awareness, then remember the Master: that Lord alone is true (and eternal).
O Nanak, serve the True Guru, board (his) ship, and cross the terrifying world-ocean.
318.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Fools proudly wear clothes as fine as the air.
O Nanak, (those clothes) do not go along (at the end); they burn up and turn to ashes.
318.6: They alone are saved in the world whom the True One has kept safe.
Seeing the faces of those who have tasted the Lord's Amrit, one comes to (true) life.
In the company of the Saadhs, lust, anger, greed and attachment are consumed.
God has shown his own mercy; the Lord himself has tested (and accepted them).
O Nanak, (his) wonders cannot be known; no one can perceive (them).
318.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, that day alone is lovely on which God comes to mind.
The day on which the Supreme Lord is forgotten, cursed is that season, however fair.
318.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, (make) friends with him in whose hands is everything.
False friends are they who do not walk a single step with (you).
318.9: The Naam is Amrit, the treasure; O brothers, come together and drink it.
In remembering it there is peace, and every thirst is quenched.
Serve the Guru, the Supreme Lord, and no hunger remains.
All desires are fulfilled, and the deathless state is attained.
O Supreme Lord, you alone are as great as you; Nanak has come to your refuge.
318.10: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have seen (God) in every place; no place is empty (of him).
O Nanak, they have found the purpose (of life) who have met the True Guru.
319.1: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As the flash of lightning, so is the way of the world.
O Nanak, this alone is the lovely thing: repeating the Name of that Master.
319.2: For all the searching of the Simritis and Shastras, no one has known (his) worth.
The one who joins the Saadh Sangat enjoys the Lord's love.
The True Name of the Creator, the all-pervading Being: this is the mine of jewels.
One on whose forehead it is written, that mortal remembers the Lord.
(O God,) let the True Name be given as provisions (for the journey): (this is) Nanak's welcome as a guest.
319.3: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Within is anxiety, while to the eye (one looks) happy; (one's) hunger never leaves at all.
O Nanak, no one's pain has been removed without the True Name.
319.4: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Robbed are those caravans that did not load (the goods of) Truth.
O Nanak, well done to those who, meeting the Guru, have recognised the One (Lord).
319.5: Where the Saadhs sit, that place is beautiful.
They serve their all-powerful (Lord), and all evil is destroyed.
O Supreme Lord, (you are) the uplifter of the fallen: so the Sants say, (and) so says the Veda.
To love devotion is your age-old way, and it holds good in every age.
Nanak begs for (your) Name alone, which is dear to (his) mind and body.
319.6: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(When) the sparrow chirps, the dawn breaks, and (the cool breeze) blows in many waves,
O Nanak, the Sants, steeped in the love of the Naam, take on a wondrous form.
319.7: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Joy is in those homes and mansions alone where you, (O God,) come to mind.
O Nanak, all the glories of the world are false friends.
319.8: The wealth of the Lord is the true capital; only a rare one has known it.
O brothers, it comes only to the one to whom the Maker gives it.
The servant dyed in the Lord's love blossoms within, in mind and body.
(He) has sung (the Lord's) praises in the Saadh Sangat, and has consumed all his faults.
O Nanak, he alone has truly lived who has recognised the One (Lord).
319.9: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The pods of the ak (swallow-wort) look lovely (as long as they) hang at the plant's neck;
O Nanak, (when) separation and parting from their master (the plant) come, (they burst) into a thousand tufts.
319.10: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who forget (the Lord) are as good as dead, yet they cannot die outright.
Turned away from Ram, (they writhe) like a thief upon the stake.
319.11: The One God alone is the treasure of peace; he is heard to be imperishable.
He fills the water, the land and the sky; in every heart dwells the Lord, so it is said.
In high and low alike he is the same; he himself has become the worm and the elephant.
Friends, companions, sons and kin are all brought forth by him.
The one to whom Nanak (the Guru), well pleased, gives the Name has enjoyed the Lord's love.
319.12: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who do not forget (the Lord) with every breath and every morsel, in whose minds is the mantra of the Lord's Name:
O Nanak, they alone are blessed; such a one alone is the perfect Sant.
319.13: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who) wanders about through all the eight watches, in the torment of (finding) food,
how can he escape falling into Dozakh, when the Rasul does not dwell in his mind?
320.1: Serve that (Guru), O mortals, who holds the Name (of the Lord) in his lap.
(Thus) you will live at ease here, and hereafter (the Name) goes along with (you).
Build the house of true dharma, setting up a pillar that cannot be shaken.
Take the shelter of Narayan, who upholds both faith and the world.
O Nanak, the one who has grasped the Lord's feet keeps firm hold of his place at his court.
320.2: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The beggar begs for alms: give, my Beloved.
You are the Giver, the Bountiful One; I remember you always.
(Your) measureless storehouses never run out at all.
O Nanak, the Shabad is infinite; it has set everything right.
320.3: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Learn the Shabad, dear ones: it is the support from birth to death.
O Nanak, remembering the One, faces stay bright and one is ever at peace.
320.4: There (in that house of true dharma) the Lord's Amrit is shared out, which makes (all) happy.
(Those who drink it) are not set on the road of Jam, and they do not have to die again.
The one who has come to taste the savour of love: that one alone has the strength to hold it.
(There) the Saadhs utter the Bani, (as if) springs of Amrit were flowing.
Nanak lives by beholding the sight (of them), and keeps (the Name) enshrined within his mind.
320.5: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When the perfect True Guru is served, sorrows are destroyed.
O Nanak, when the Name is worshipped, (life's) purpose is fulfilled.
320.6: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The One by remembering whom troubles depart, and bliss and joy come to dwell:
O Nanak, let us repeat (the Name of) that Lord always; may the Name not be forgotten even for an instant.
320.7: Those who have found the Lord, Har Har: how can I count their glory?
Whoever falls at the refuge of the Saadhs is set free, bound though he was.
He sings the praises of the Imperishable One, and does not burn in the womb of births.
The Guru, the Supreme Lord, the Lord, meets him; reading (of the Lord) and understanding, he comes to rest in stillness.
O Nanak, he has found that Master, the Lord, who is inaccessible and unfathomable.
320.8: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O mortal,) you do not do your own (true) work, and you roam the world headstrong.
O Nanak, once the Name is forgotten, what kind of peace can there be?
320.9: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The bitterness of the poison (of Maya) is in all; it clings (to everyone) in the world.
O Nanak, the servant (of God) has reflected and found that the Lord's Name (alone) is sweet.
320.10: This is the mark of the Saadh: meeting him, one swims across.
Jam's servant does not come near, and one does not die ever again.
The world-ocean, this world full of poison: one crosses over to its far shore.
Weave in your mind the garland of the Lord's virtues: (thus) the Lord takes all filth away.
O Nanak, (they) remain united with the Beloved, the Supreme Lord, Narhari.
320.11: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, approved is the coming of those in whose minds the Lord has come to dwell.
Idle talk, empty as chaff, is of no use, my friend.
320.12: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord God, all-pervading, inaccessible, wondrous, has come into view to the one
who, O Nanak, by the perfect Guru's grace, has made the Name of Ram his wealth.
321.1: Deceit does not work with the Master; through greed and attachment (people) come to ruin.
They do evil deeds, asleep in the intoxication of Maya.
Again and again they are made to wander through births, and are abandoned on the road of Jam.
They reap what they themselves have done, yoked to sorrow.
O Nanak, once the Name is forgotten, every season is ill.
321.2: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Rising, sitting and sleeping, (such a one) has the same unbroken peace.
O Nanak, when the Name is praised, mind and body become cool.
321.3: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Smeared with greed, (the world) ever roams about; no one does what is truly for his own good.
O Nanak, the one whom the Guru meets: in that one's mind he (the Lord) comes to dwell.
321.4: All (worldly) things are bitter; the Name of the True One (alone) is sweet.
Those servants of the Lord have known (its) savour, the Saadhs who have tasted it and seen.
In the mind of that one alone does (the Name) come to dwell, for whom the Supreme Lord has so written.
(To that one) the one stainless Lord (is seen) pervading all, and the love of another is slain.
With palms joined Nanak begs (this of) the Lord; God gives (it) when he is pleased.
321.5: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That asking is the best which asks for the One alone.
O Nanak, other talk, empty of the Master, is worthless.
321.6: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One whose mind is pierced with love (of the Lord), such a knower (of God), is rare indeed.
Such a Sant is the uniter (with the Lord), O Nanak; (he) makes the path smooth and level.
321.7: Serve him alone, O my soul, the Giver, the Forgiver.
Remembering Govind, all sins are destroyed.
The Saadh (the Guru) has shown the way to the Lord: let us repeat the Guru's mantra.
(Then) all the tastes of Maya (seem) insipid, and the Lord is dear to the mind.
O Nanak, meditate on the Supreme God, who has given (you) life.
321.8: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The season for (sowing) the True Name has come; whoever sows, he eats (its fruit).
O Nanak, (it) is his alone in whose lot (it) has come written.
321.9: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If one must ask, (let it be) for the One True (Name); (but it comes only to the one) to whom (God) himself gives it when pleased.
That (Name), eating which the mind is satisfied, is, O Nanak, the Master's gift.
321.10: They alone earn profit in the world whose capital is the wealth of the Lord.
They do not know the love of another; their hope is in the True One.
They have served the One, the Unshakable; all else is perishable.
One who forgets the Supreme Lord: (every) breath of his is in vain.
Hugging (his) servants to his breast, (God) has saved them; Nanak is a sacrifice (to him).
321.11: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord gave the command, and the rain fell, gently, of its own accord.
Grain and wealth sprang up in plenty; the earth was filled, fully content.
(Such a one) utters (the Lord's) virtues for ever and ever, and pain and poverty have vanished.
What was written from before has been received; (it) has come by his will.
The Supreme God has given life; O Nanak, meditate on him.
321.12: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The state of true life (lies in this): to remember the One alone, (the Lord) beyond desire.
There is no other place; how else can (the mind) take comfort?
(I) have looked at the whole world: there is no peace without the Name.
Body and wealth will turn to ashes; only a rare one knows (this).
Pleasures, beauty and tastes are in vain; what are you doing, O mortal?
The one whom (God) himself leads astray has not known (his) power.
Those dyed in (the Lord's) love sing of the True One, (the Lord) beyond desire.
Says Nanak: if (beings) are pleasing to you, (they come) to your refuge, at your door.
322.1: There is no birth and death for those who cling to the Lord's hem.
Awake in the Lord's Kirtan, they have been approved while still living.
Those who have found the Saadh Sangat are the truly fortunate.
Once the Name is forgotten, life is cursed: (it) snaps like a raw thread.
O Nanak, holier than lakhs and crores of Prayags is the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh.
322.2: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Like the earth in its beauty, its grass studded with jewels (of dew), is the mind in which the Lord, the Being of love, has come to dwell.
All tasks become easy when Guru Nanak, the True Guru, is pleased.
322.3: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Roaming and roaming in the ten directions, over waters, mountains and forests,
wherever the kite saw a carcass, there it came down and settled.
322.4: From whom all comforts and fruits are sought: may I live by that True One.
May I see the Supreme Lord close at hand, and meditate on the Name of the One.
Becoming the dust (of the feet) of all, may I merge in the Lord.
May I cause no being pain, and go (to my true) home with honour.
May Nanak tell (all) of the Creator, the Being who makes the fallen pure.
322.5: Salok, a Doha, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have made the One my Friend, who is mighty with every power.
My soul is cut in pieces as a sacrifice (to him); the Lord is the (true) treasure of mind and body.
322.6: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If you take (my) hand, dear Beloved, I will never let you go.
Those who forsake the Lord are the wicked; they fall into the (piercing) torment of Dozakh.
322.7: The Lord in whose house are all treasures: whatever he does comes to pass.
The Sants live by repeating (his Name) over and over; he washes off (their) filth of sins.
(Those) in whose hearts (his) lotus feet dwell: he takes away all (their) troubles.
The one whom the perfect Guru meets does not weep (in the round of) dying and being born.
Nanak thirsts greatly for the sight of God; (God) grants (it) out of (his) grace.
322.8: Salok Dakhna, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If you cast off even a little of (your) doubt and love the Beloved alone,
then wherever you go, there he is present.
322.9: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Players of the stick game (khundi), they mount a fine horse and grip gun-butts;
with a chicken's flight, they stir up their hearts to (fly) with swans.
322.10: One who utters the Lord('s Name) with the tongue and listens to it with the ears is saved, O friend.
Pure are those hands that write the Lord's praise with devotion.
(It is as if) that one has bathed at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage and done every good deed.
Such ones are saved from the world-ocean, and have won the fortress of Maya.
O Nanak, serve the infinite Beloved, who has attached (them) to his hem and saved them.
323.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Wretched affairs are a losing trade, (when through them) the One does not come to mind.
O Nanak, those very bodies split open, (the bodies of those) who forget the Master.
323.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
From a ghost, he, the Creator, has made (one) a god.
He has saved all the Sikhs; God has set their tasks right.
Seizing the slanderers, he has dashed them to the ground; false (they stand) at his court.
Great is the God of Nanak: he himself fashions (all) and puts (them) right.
323.3: God is without end; there is no limit to him at all; everything is his doing.
The Master is beyond reach and beyond the senses, the support of (all) beings.
Giving (his) hand, he protects (all), and does the feeding and sustaining (of all).
He himself is merciful and forgiving; repeating (the Name of) the True One, (beings) cross over.
(O Lord,) whatever pleases you is good; servant Nanak is in your refuge.
323.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those whose (Master) is that God are left with no hunger of any kind.
O Nanak, by clinging to (his) feet everyone is saved.
323.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The beggar asks for the Name every day, and the Master grants (his plea).
O Nanak, (the one whose) patron (jajman) is the Supreme God has no hunger at all.
323.6: (The minstrel's) mind is dyed with Govind; the True One('s Name) is (his) food and clothing.
Love fixed on the Lord's Name: these are (his) elephants and horses.
To meditate (on God) and never turn his face away: (this is his) kingdom, lands and abundant joy.
The minstrel begs at God's door, and never leaves that door.
O Nanak, this is the longing in (his) mind and body: he yearns for God every day.
323.7: Raag Gauri, the hymns of the Bhagats.
There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Gauri Guareri, fourteen Chaupade of Sri Kabir Ji.
Now, as I burned, I have found the water of Ram.
The water of Ram has cooled my burning body.
One goes off to the forests to subdue the mind,
(but) that water is not found without the Lord (Bhagvant).
The fire that has burned gods and men:
from its burning the water of Ram has saved (his) servants.
In the world-ocean, (become for them) an ocean of peace,
they go on drinking, and the water never runs short.
the water of Ram has quenched my thirst.
323.8: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
O Madho, my thirst for the water (of your Name) does not leave;
in the water, a fire (of longing) has flared up all the more.
You are the ocean, and I the fish of (that) water:
in the water I live; without the water I waste away.
You are the cage, and I your little parrot:
what harm can Jam, the cat, do me?
You are the tree, and I the bird (in it);
unfortunate (that I am), I have not had the sight of you.
You are the True Guru, and I a new disciple;
says Kabir: meet me, (now) at the last hour.
324.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
When I came to know (God) as the One alone, (in all),
why then have people taken it ill?
I am without honour; I have lost my own honour:
let none of you come following in my track.
If I am bad, I am bad within my own mind;
I have no partnership or fellowship with anyone.
Of honour and dishonour I feel no shame;
you will know when your own pretence is laid bare.
Says Kabir: honour is (to be) accepted by the Lord;
leave all else, and worship Ram alone.
324.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
If union (with God) were found by roaming about naked,
every deer of the forest would be liberated.
What (comes) of going naked, what of wearing skins,
when you do not recognise the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram)?
If attainment were won by shaving the head,
why has no sheep gone to liberation?
If one could cross over by holding back the seed, O brother,
why has the eunuch not attained the supreme state?
Says Kabir: listen, O men, O brothers:
without the Name of Ram, who has ever attained liberation?
324.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(Those who) bathe at evening and at dawn
are like the frogs in the water.
If there is no love for Ram, Ram (in them),
they all go into the hands of Dharam Raj.
(Those who,) in love with the body, put on many guises
have no compassion in them, not even in a dream.
Many clever men recite the four Vedas,
(but only) the holy find peace in this ocean of strife.
Says Kabir: why go on at length?
Let us leave everything and drink the supreme essence (of the Name).
324.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Of what use is chanting, austerity, fasting or worship
to one in whose heart is the love of another?
O people, let the mind be fixed on Madho;
by cleverness Chaturbhuj (the four-armed Lord) is not found.
Cast off greed and doing things for show;
cast off lust, anger and pride.
Performing rites, (people) are bound in self-conceit;
Says Kabir: (he) is found through devotion;
with an innocent love, Raghurai is met.
324.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
In the dwelling of the womb there is no family and no caste;
all have come into being from the seed of Brahm (God).
Tell me, O pandit, since when have you been Brahmins?
Do not waste your life calling (yourselves) Brahmins over and over.
If you are a Brahmin, born of a Brahmin woman,
then why did you not come (into the world) by some other way?
How are you Brahmins, and how are we Shudras?
How is there blood in us, and how milk in you?
Says Kabir: whoever reflects on Brahm (God)
is the one we call a Brahmin.
325.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
In darkness, (forgetting God,) no one ever sleeps in peace;
king and pauper both alike weep.
As long as the tongue does not utter (the Name of) Ram,
(people) will go on being born and dying, and weeping.
(Maya is) as the shade of a tree is seen to be;
when the breath of life is gone, tell me, whose is Maya then?
As the sound is absorbed into the instrument (when the playing stops),
how can anyone fathom the secret of the dead?
As the swan stays close to the lake, so death stays close to the body;
drink the elixir of Ram, O Kabir.
325.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The creation is of the Light (God's making); the light (of mind) in the creation
bears fruits of glass and of pearl.
Which is that home which may be called free of fear,
where fear runs away and one may live fearless?
At a river's bank or a place of pilgrimage the mind is not set at ease;
(people there) remain entangled in good deeds and bad.
Sin and virtue: the two are alike.
In your own home (within) is the paras (the touchstone that turns iron to gold, the Lord); give up (seeking) other qualities.
O Kabir, do not turn sullenly from the Name of the Lord beyond the qualities (nirgun);
engage this (mind), and stay absorbed in this (Name).
325.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Those people (who say they) have known the One beyond measure and beyond the mind
have entered Baikunth by talk alone.
I do not know where Baikunth is;
(yet) all say: we must go there, go there.
By saying and being told, the mind is not set at ease;
the mind is satisfied (only) when Haumai has departed from it.
As long as there is hope of Baikunth in the mind,
there is no dwelling at (the Lord's) feet.
Says Kabir: what more is there to say of this?
The Saadh Sangat is Baikunth itself.
325.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(A being) comes into being, takes bodily form, and having taken form, passes away;
while our eyes look on, this world is going.
Do you not die of shame, saying: this house is mine?
At the end, nothing at all is yours.
With countless efforts the body is reared;
(yet) when death comes, it is burned with fire.
The body whose limbs are rubbed with perfume and sandalwood:
that body burns along with the wood.
Says Kabir: listen, O men of worth:
(this) form will perish, with all the world looking on.
325.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Grieve (only) if you yourself were to live on.
I shall not die; it is the world that will die;
now I have met the Giver of life.
(One) makes this body fragrant with perfumes;
in those pleasures (he) forgets (the Lord of) supreme bliss.
(The body is) one little well, (the five senses) five women who draw its water;
the defeated intellect draws (water) with a broken rope.
Says Kabir: I have weighed one thought in my mind:
(now) there is neither that little well nor the drawers of water.
325.6: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
As the unmoving and the moving, as worms and moths,
(we) have taken countless births of many kinds.
Many such homes (bodies) have we lived in
when, O Ram, we came (again and again) into the womb.
(We have been) yogis, men of restraint, ascetics and celibates;
sometimes kings beneath the royal canopy, sometimes beggars.
The Saakats die, (but) the Sants all live:
with their tongues they drink the elixir of Ram.
Says Kabir: O God, show mercy;
worn out, we have fallen (at your door); now grant (us) the perfect (state).
326.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji, written together with (words of) the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Such a wonder Kabir has seen:
mistaking it for curd, one churns water.
The donkey grazes on green shoots;
rising each day, it laughs and brays, and (at last) dies.
leaping and leaping it grazes, and falls into the netherworld (Rasatal).
Says Kabir: the play has come into the open:
the ewe is ever suckling at her lamb.
Dwelling on Ram, understanding has come to light;
says Kabir: the Guru has given (this) insight.
326.2: Raag Gauri, Panchpade of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(People say:) like a fish that has left the water and come out,
(so) I was empty of austerity in my former birth.
Now tell me, O Ram, what will my state be?
I have left Banaras; (is it true that) my wits have grown small?
(They say:) he wasted his whole life in Shiva's city (Kashi),
(and) at the hour of death he got up and came to Magahar.
For many years (he) did austerities at Kashi;
(yet) when death came, (he became) a dweller of Magahar.
(But I) have held Kashi and Magahar to be alike;
with shallow devotion, how will (anyone) cross over?
Says (Kabir): the gurus, Ganesh, Shiva and everyone know (it):
Kabir has died dwelling on Sri Ram.
326.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The body whose limbs are rubbed with perfume and sandalwood:
that body burns along with the wood.
What greatness is there in this body and wealth?
They lie on the earth, (left) on this side; they do not go (with you).
Those who spend the night in sleep and the day at work,
and do not take the Lord's Name for a single moment;
who hold (the falcon's) cord in their hand and chew betel in their mouth:
when death comes, they are bound fast like a thief.
One who, through the Guru's teaching, sings the Lord's praises with deep relish
finds peace dwelling on Ram, Ram alone.
The one in whom (God), by his grace, implants the Naam firmly:
in him he makes the sweet fragrance of Har Har dwell.
Says Kabir: remember (him), O blind one;
Ram is true; all (worldly) business is false.
326.4: Raag Gauri, Tipade Chartuke of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(Those who were) Jams have turned and become (forms of) Ram;
sorrows have perished, and peace has come to rest.
Enemies have turned and become friends;
the Saakats have turned and become good men at heart.
Now I take everything as well-being;
peace came when I came to know Gobind.
In the body there were millions of afflictions;
they have turned into peace, and samadhi in Sahaj.
(The mind) recognises its own self, and (sees) him alone, all in all;
no disease, nor the three fevers, afflict (it now).
Now the mind has turned and become (one with) the Eternal;
this I knew when I died while still alive.
Says Kabir: I am merged in peace and in Sahaj;
I neither fear, nor make others afraid.
327.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
When the body has died, into which home does the soul go?
(It stays) steeped, through the Shabad, in the Lord beyond (Maya), the Unending.
Whoever has known Ram, he alone has recognised (this joy),
as a mute's mind is satisfied with sugar (and he cannot tell of it).
Such wisdom Banwari (the Lord himself) imparts:
O mind, hold the breath steady in the Sukhmana channel.
Take such a Guru that you need not take another;
enjoy such a state that you need enjoy no other;
hold such meditation that you need hold no other;
die in such a way that you need not die again.
Turning (my mind) back, I join the Ganga and the Jamuna;
without water, I bathe at (their) confluence within the mind.
To look on (all) with even eyes: this is (my) way of dealing;
having reflected on the Essence, what need of other reflection?
Like water, fire, air, earth and sky
is the life I live, (abiding) near the Lord.
Says Kabir: I meditate on the Niranjan;
I go to that home from which I shall not come back again.
327.2: Raag Gauri, Tipade of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(Ram) is not won by weighing out gold;
I have bought Ram at the price of my mind.
Now I know Ram as my own;
my mind has come to trust (in him), naturally, in Sahaj.
Brahma, telling of (him) over and over, did not find his end;
through devotion to Ram, (he) has come to (my) home while I sat (there).
Says Kabir: I have given up the restless intellect;
devotion to Ram alone is my own share.
327.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The death that has struck terror into the whole world:
(what) that death (is), the Guru's Shabad has made plain (to me).
Now how can I die? My mind has embraced (that) death (to self).
Those who have not known Ram die and die (again), and depart.
(but) one who dies in Sahaj, he alone becomes immortal.
Says Kabir: bliss has arisen in my mind;
doubt has gone; the supreme bliss remains.
327.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
There is no (one) place (of the pain); where shall I put the remedy?
Searching the body, I do not find the place.
Only the one it has struck knows the pain:
(the pain of) the sharp-pointed arrows of devotion to Ram.
I see all the brides alike;
how am I to know which one the Husband holds dear?
Says Kabir: she on whose forehead good fortune is (written):
her the Husband, leaving all (others), comes to meet.
328.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
One who has such a Master as the Lord, O brother:
to (his door) go liberations without number, to plead.
Now say: O Ram, (my) trust is in you;
then why be beholden to anyone?
He who bears the weight of the three worlds:
Says Kabir: I have weighed one thought in my mind:
what can (the child) do if the mother herself gives poison?
328.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Without sat (faithfulness), how can a woman be a sati?
O pandit, reflect in your heart and see.
Without love, how can affection take hold?
As long as (Maya's) relish (remains), there is no love (for the Lord).
One who, in his heart, holds the Shah's wife (Maya) to be true
will not meet Ramaiya (the all-pervading Lord), even in a dream.
She who gives over body, mind, wealth, home and self (to the Husband):
she alone is the happy wife, says Kabir.
328.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The whole world is in the grip of the poison of Maya;
this poison has drowned the whole family.
O man, why have you sunk your boat in the shallows?
You have broken (your love) with the Lord and joined it to the poison.
Gods and men are burnt up, for a fire (of craving) has broken out;
the water is near at hand, yet the beast (man) will not make the effort to drink it.
Through remembering and remembering, the water (of the Name) has sprung forth;
says Kabir: that water is pure.
328.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The family in which no son reflects on divine wisdom —
why did his mother not become a widow?
The man who has not practised devotion to Ram —
why did that sinner not die at birth?
Many, many pregnancies have miscarried; why was this one spared?
He lives in the world like a leper with wasted arms.
Says Kabir: those who are handsome and fair of form
are, without the Name, like the hunchbacked and the ugly.
328.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The servants who take the Name of the Master —
to them I am ever a sacrifice.
One who sings the praises of the pure Lord is pure;
that brother is dear to my mind.
Those in whose hearts Ram dwells in fullness —
I am the dust of their lotus feet.
A weaver by caste, but steadfast of mind,
Kabir, in Sahaj, ever in Sahaj, utters (the Lord's) praises.
328.6: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
My still is in the sky (of the raised mind), and from it the sweet nectar drips;
to gather this supreme essence, the body has become the firewood.
That one is called intoxicated in Sahaj
who drinks the elixir of Ram through reflection on divine wisdom.
When Sahaj, the woman who pours the wine, comes and meets (one),
then, intoxicated in bliss, (one's life) passes night and day.
When, recognising (him), (I) fixed my mind on the Niranjan,
says Kabir: then (I) attained the inner experience (of God).
328.7: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Whatever the mind's nature, it pervades the whole mind;
(so) by killing the mind, what perfection has anyone established?
Who is that silent sage who kills the mind?
Tell me, by killing the mind, whom does he carry across?
Everyone speaks from within the mind;
without killing the mind, there is no devotion.
Says Kabir: for one who knows this secret,
(his) mind becomes Madhusudan, the God who lights the three worlds.
329.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Those stars that are seen in the sky —
Tell me, O pandit, on whom does the sky rest?
Only a fortunate one, wise of understanding, understands (this).
The sun and the moon give light;
in all is spread the expanse of Brahm (God).
Says Kabir: he alone will know (this)
in whose heart is Ram, and in whose mouth is Ram alone.
329.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The Smriti, O brother, is the daughter of the Veda;
she has come bringing a chain and a rope.
She herself has bound her own city (those who follow her);
(holding them) in the noose of attachment, she has aimed the arrow of death.
(This noose) cannot be cut, cut as one may, nor will it break;
she has become a she-serpent, and devours the world.
She who has plundered the whole world before my eyes —
says Kabir: I have escaped (her) by uttering (the Name of) Ram.
329.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
I put the halter (on the horse of the mind) and fit it with the bridle;
with the saddle of (seeing the Lord in) all, I gallop (it) through the sky.
Let us ride (the horse of) reflection on our own (true self),
and set our foot in the stirrup of Sahaj.
Come, (my horse,) let me take you and carry you across to Baikunth;
if you balk, I shall strike (you) with the whip of love.
who stay apart from the Vedas and the Kateb.
329.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The mouth with which the five ambrosial foods were eaten —
to that mouth, before (one's own people's) eyes, the burning brand is put.
O Ram, my King, cut away this one pain of mine:
the burning in the fire, and the dwelling in the womb.
The body comes to ruin in many ways and manners:
some burn it, some bury it in the earth.
Says Kabir: O Lord, let (me) see (your) feet;
after that, why not send Jam, if you will?
329.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(The Master) himself is the fire, and himself the wind;
if the Master burns (one), who can save?
While repeating Ram, what if the body should burn?
The mind remains absorbed in the Name of Ram.
What of anyone's is burnt? Who suffers loss?
Saringpani is playing, like an actor in his play.
Says Kabir: utter (just) these two words:
if the Master (so wills), he will keep (me) safe.
329.6: Raag Gauri, Dupade of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
I have not set my mind on the meditation of Yoga;
without detachment, there is no release from Maya.
when the support of the Name of Ram is not there?
Says Kabir: I search (as far as) the heavens,
yet I see no other equal to Ram.
330.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The head on which (one) ties the turban, arranging it with care —
that head the crows will dress with their beaks.
Why take pride in this body and wealth?
Why do you not hold fast to the Name of Ram?
Says Kabir: listen, O my mind,
this same will be your state too.
The thirty-five Pade of Gauri Guareri.
330.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, an Ashtapadi of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
In asking for comfort, pain comes to meet one;
I do not care to ask for that comfort.
The attention is still on the poison of Maya, with hope of comforts;
how, (then,) shall there be a dwelling in Ram the King?
Of this comfort even Shiv and Brahma were afraid;
that comfort we have taken to be true.
Sanak and his brothers, the sage Narad, and Shesh Nag:
even they did not see the mind within the body.
Let someone search out this mind, O brother:
when the body falls away, where is the mind absorbed?
By the Guru's grace, Jaidev and Namdev —
these have known (it), through the love of devotion.
For this mind there is no coming and going;
one whose doubt is gone has recognised the True One.
This mind has no form or outline at all;
it came to be by Hukam, and understanding the Hukam, it merges (in the Lord).
Rare is the one who knows the secret of this mind;
absorbed in this mind, (one) becomes Sukhdev (bliss and light itself).
The Soul is One, and (it is in) all bodies;
Kabir remembers this Mind (the One in all).
330.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Those who stay awake night and day in the Name of the One —
so many of them, their attention attuned (to it), have reached perfection.
Seekers at their disciplines, Siddhas and all the sages have failed;
the One Name alone is the Kalp tree (that grants every wish), and it carries (them) across.
Those whom the Lord has drawn (to himself) do not become other (than him);
says Kabir: (they) have recognised the Name of Ram.
330.4: Raag Gauri, and Sorath too: the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
O shameless soul, have you no shame?
Forsaking the Lord, why do you go to (the door of) another?
it does not become that servant to go to another's house.
the Lord is ever with (you), not far away.
He at whose feet even Kavla (Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth) has taken refuge —
tell me, O man, what is lacking in his house?
is all-powerful, (our) own Master, and the Giver.
Says Kabir: in the world he alone is complete
in whose heart there is no other (but the Lord).
331.1: Who is anyone's son, and who anyone's father?
Who dies, and who causes (another) grief?
The Lord, the cheat, has given the world his cheat's drug;
parted from the Lord, how can I live, O my mother?
Who is anyone's husband, and who anyone's wife?
Reflect within the body, and grasp this truth.
Says Kabir: (my) mind is won over by the cheat;
the drug's spell is gone, (for I) have recognised the cheat.
331.2: Now Ram, the King, has become my helper;
cutting away birth and death, I have attained the supreme state.
He has joined me to the Saadh Sangat,
and set me free from the five enemies.
With my tongue I chant the Naam, the nectar of life;
he has made me his own servant, without price.
The True Guru has done (me) a great kindness:
he has drawn me out of the world-ocean.
Love for (the Lord's) lotus feet has taken hold (of me);
Gobind dwells in my mind day after day.
The live coal of Maya's burning heat has gone out;
there is contentment in the mind, and the Naam is (its) support.
